articleTitle: In-memory processing paradigm for bitwise logic operations in STT-MRAM
abstract: In current big data era, the limited data bandwidth (memory wall) between the processor and the memory becomes one of the most critical bottlenecks for conventional Von-Newman computer architecture. In this work, we propose a cost-efficient IMP solution in STT-MRAM without adding any processing units on the memory chip. The key idea behind the proposed IMP solution is to exploit the peripheral circuitry already existing inside memory (or with minimal changes) to perform bitwise logic operations.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis and optimization of dynamic charging coils for roadway-powered electric vehicles
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) show significant potentials to penetrate renewable energies into our daily life.

articleTitle: Optimal design of the wound field synchronous reluctance machines to improve torque by increasing saliency ratio
abstract: Salient pole wound field synchronous machines (WFSMs) are widely used for various electric power generation, such as hydro and wind generators [1], because there is free of permanent magnet and it can be directly controlled by the DC winding. In this paper, design optimization techniques for the WFSM with single flux barrier configuration were investigated and then optimized the width of flux barrier and location of the single flux barrier by the Kriging Method and Genetic Algorithm. To verify the contribution of the optimized model, the basic and proposed models are adopted for comparison by a 2-D finite element method (FEM).

articleTitle: A novel three-phase compact saturated core fault current limiter
abstract: The rapid development of large scale power system and the implementation of dispersed generation have led to the increasing level of fault current which may be over the breakers' operating limit threatening the safety of power system.

articleTitle: Portable rotational electromagnetic energy harvester for IoT
abstract: This paper presents a development and fabrication of a rotational electromagnetic energy harvesting (EH) system.The electromagnetic harvester is driven mechanically by pushing a button. The energy harvester converts the linear translation of the button into rotation with a rotational speed of about 1000rpm. The electromagnetic part of the harvester consists of a multilayer planar coils embedded into PCB and of multipole NdFeB permanent magnets. The energy harvester device generates maximal energy of about 20mJ. The maximal open circuit voltage up to 4V is realized.

articleTitle: Parameter calculation and analysis of a novel wind power generator
abstract: Brushless doubly fed generator (BDFG) has many benefits such as no brush or slip rings, robust structure, lower operation and maintenance costs as well as requiring a smaller capacity converter, which make it an attractive alternative as a wind turbine generator [1]-[2].

articleTitle: Time-division multiplexing wireless power transfer for separately excited DC motor drives
abstract: Wireless power transfer (WPT) system is becoming popular for industrial application [1].

articleTitle: A novel consequent-pole hybrid excited vernier permanent-magnet machine for EV/HEV applications
abstract: The paper proposes a novel consequent-pole HEVPMM (CP-HEVPMM) with DC field windings located between flux modulation poles which can easily adjust flux density. The CP-HEVPMM could operate at low-speed with high torque density and at high-speed with flux-weakening controlling due to adopt the vernier machine structure and DC field windings, respectively. In order to minimize the torque fluctuation, the preliminary designs including various combinations of the stator slots and rotor poles will be discussed in this paper. The finite element method (FEM) is used to analyze electromagnetic performance of CP-HEVPMM including back-electromagnetic force (back-EMF), cogging torque, and average torque.

articleTitle: Design of hybrid thrust Magnetic bearing for heavy rotating shaft considering self-weight compensation according to axial load
abstract: In this paper, the design and analysis of a HTMB for a 6kW 60,000-rpm-class spindle for micro-drilling machine are presented. This paper is divided into three main parts: the design of HTMB, the influence of self-weight that changes according to the axial load, and the redesign of HTMB considering self-weight compensation according to axial load. The first part focuses on the design of HTMB which use a finite element method (FEM), deals with a general design that does not consider self-weight according to axial load. The second part is based on the validation of the initial designs by experiments using a manufactured HTMB, and deals with the influence of self-weight that changes according to the axial load. Finally, redesign of HTMB for compensation self-weight with axial load, and validation of the results by the two-dimensional FEM, and then by experiments using a manufactured model. In a future study, a more specific comparison with an accurate design method in consideration of the selfweight with axial load, will be thoroughly investigated for its contribution to related researches and industrial applications.

articleTitle: Operator safety and field focality in shielded transcranial magnetic stimulation
abstract: Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) is a medical treatment aimed at modulating the activity of cerebral targets, through pulses of electric field generated inside the brain.

articleTitle: A new anisotropic vector hysteresis model based on play hysterons
abstract: Summary form only given. The phenomenon of isotropic and anisotropic magnetic hysteresis has been observed for a long time in various magnetic materials which are widely used in electrical devices. Herein, an improved isotropic vector play model was introduced based on the play hysteron with one isotropic vector play operator. This operator returns the reversible magnetic field component h<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">re</sub> from its initial value h<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">re0</sub> and the applied field h. When the applied field is located inside the circle, the returned reversible field component keeps the same as its initial value. When the applied field is located outside the circle, the returned reversible field component is determined based on the vector diagram. The difference between the ordinary vector play model and the improved vector play model is: for the ordinary vector play model, the radius of the circle is constant, however, for the improved vector play model, the radius is a function of the reversible field component. The radius will approach to zero when the field is fully saturated so that the rotational loss is zero because the flux density vector is parallel with the applied field vector. The parameter of this improved play model is the function of the radius varying with the reversible field component, which can be easily identified from the major hysteresis loop. For an anisotropic hysteresis material, the magnetic hysteresis property in one principal axis may be different from those in other principal axes. When an alternating magnetic field h(t) is applied in a principal direction, a lagging alternating flux density b(t), in the same direction as h(t), will be produced, leading to a hysteresis loop. The hysteresis loops in different principal directions could be different. Therefore, the magnetic hysteresis loops in all principal directions are essential for constructing an anisotropic vector hysteresis model. Some existing anisotropic hysteresis models require not only the magnetic hysteresis loops in all principal directions, but also hysteresis loops in some specified directions which are difficult to be measured. In this paper, an anisotropic hysteresis model is presented based on the isotropic hysteresis model. This model requires only the major hysteresis loop in each principal direction. The anisotropic hysteresis behaviors in all other directions can be described by the three (for 3D) or two (for 2D) hysteresis properties of the principal directions. This model uses one isotropic vector play hysteron, which is identified from the major hysteresis loop, in each principal direction. The vector play hysterons in all principal directions are based on the same vector flux density input, where hx(b), hy(b), and hz(b) represent the responses of isotropic vector play hysterons of the x-, y-, and z-axes, respectively, and i, j, and k are the unit vectors of the x-, y-, and z-axes, respectively. For the sake of generalization, the proposed anisotropic hysteresis model also takes the lamination effects into account. With the lamination effects, the resultant magnetic behavior is anisotropic even though the steel material possesses isotropic hysteresis properties. To validate the proposed anisotropic hysteresis model, a numerical experiment is set up. The major hysteresis loops in all principal directions of a laminated stack with isotropic hysteresis properties are numerically measured and input to the anisotropic hysteresis model. Then the hysteresis behavior in some specified direction other than the principal directions is simulated by the proposed anisotropic hysteresis model, and compared with the numeric measured data. Finally, the proposed model is applied to compute the hysteresis loss of a 400W 4-pole synchronous reluctance motor with an axially-laminated rotor.

articleTitle: Comparative study of PM-assisted SynRM and IPMSM on constant power speed range for EV applications
abstract: This work analyzes and compares the performances of permanent-magnet-assisted synchronous reluctance machines (PMa-SynRM) and interior permanent magnet synchronous machine (IPMSM) on their constant power speed range (CPSR) capability for electric vehicle (EV) applications. The CPSR is a key performance index for traction motors to achieve wide speed range where the IPMSM is known to be an excellent candidate. However, a recent trend for traction motor development is to reduce the amount of rare earth magnet used due to its high cost and possible supply uncertainty. As an alternative, the PMa-SynRM possesses a higher saliency (thus higher reluctance torque) and lower PM quantity (thus lower PM torque) compared to IPMSMs. With the same power or torque output, the major distinction between these two types of machines would be the proportions of different torque components (PM and reluctance torques) due to rotor designs. The distinctive rotor designs would significantly affect the CPSR and this needs to be investigated for traction motor designs and various EV applications. Five 10 kW-30 Nm/L designs, with three IPMSMs and two PMa-SynRMs are studied. The analysis results show that the PMa-SynRMs can achieve higher peak speed despite the torque and power are lower at high speed. In contrast, the IPMSM can maintain the power beyond the base speed to achieve superior CPSR but the power drops quickly to zero at high speed. The high efficiency region appears at the mid speed range for the IPMSM but at high speed region for the PMa-SynRM due to their different PM and reluctance torque profiles. Two prototypes were tested, one being IPMSM and the other PMa-SynRM to validate the analysis results.

articleTitle: A novel dual-stator vernier permanent magnet machine
abstract: In many direct-drive applications such as servo system, wind power generation, etc., it is desirable to use motors having a high torque density at a low rotation speed without reduction gears for the improvement of noises, reliability and maintenance. Albeit that some step motors can satisfy this requirement, the torque ripple of step motors are usually large, which will lead to vibrations and reduce the control accuracy. Vernier permanent magnet (VPM) machines exhibit high torque density and small pulsating torque at low speed due to the “magnetic gearing effect” [1]-[3]. So VPM machines are promising candidates in direct-drive systems. In order to further improve the torque performances of conventional VPM machines, a novel dual-stator VPM machine will be presented and analyzed in this paper.

articleTitle: Vortex magnetization state in a GMR spin-valve type field sensor
abstract: Summary form only given. In this paper, we present a different approach by using circularly shaped elements exhibiting a different magnetization state. The magnetic vortex is one of the fundamental magnetization ground states occurring in disk-shaped thin film elements and is characterized by minimization of the demagnetizing energy at the expense of exchange energy. The state is described as free of hysteresis and planar stray-fields, and discussed as potential oscillator in spin-torque systems, memory bits and magnetic field sensors. In order to compare important parameters like resistance, magnetoresistance amplitude, sensitivity, hysteresis, critical fields like nucleation and annihilation fields in dependence on the free layer thickness and disk radius, single and arrays (10 and 1750 in number) of GMR disks have been fabricated by optical lithography and contacted.

articleTitle: Additive manufacturing of bonded NdFeB, process parameters evaluation on magnetic properties
abstract: Bonded NdFeB magnets were fabricated by an additive manufacturing (AM) technique known as selective laser sintering (SLS). A mixture of spherical isotropic powders of a NdFeB based alloy and polymeric binder (PA 12) was used as process feedstock. The amount of binder used was varied to optimize mechanical resistance and magnetic properties. Besides that, two parameters were evaluated: layer thickness and hatch spacing. In order to enhance binder activity, fabrication temperature was kept between 368K and 373K. Scanning speed and laser power were constant, 1300 mm/s and 42W, respectively. For magnetic properties evaluation, cylindrical samples with diameter and height of 10mm were produced. Magnetic properties measured in a hystograph (Brockhaus EM 1800 model) indicate that lower SLS parameters combined with lowest binder content (6 wt. %) showed higher magnetic properties, with average values for remanence (B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>) of 0,33T, intrinsic coercivity (H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cj</sub>) of 696 kA/m and maximum energy-product (BH)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</sub> of 17,1 kJ/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The obtained results were compared with those obtained for bonded magnets fabricated by pressing, using the same feedstock, for which the highest remanence and maximum energy-product were, 0,38 T and 24,1 kJ/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. In conclusion, the study showed that magnetic properties can be improved by reducing hatching space and layer thickness and also AM by SLS technique can be used to produce complex magnet shapes.

articleTitle: Structural Health Monitoring using magnetostrictive sensors
abstract: Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) of aircraft composite is required to determine the barely visible impact damage (BVID) that occurs during flight.

articleTitle: Top pinned magnetic tunnel junction stacks with high annealing tolerance for high density STT-MRAM applications
abstract: Perpendicular magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJ) are widely being researched as they are the key component in advanced spin transfer torque magnetic random access memory (STT-MRAM).

articleTitle: HTS dual-stator spoke-type linear vernier machine for leakage flux reduction
abstract: In this paper, bulk high temperature superconductor (HTS) is utilized to decrease the leakage flux in DSSLVM and improve its power factor. The proposed machine is termed as high temperature superconductor dual stator spoke type linear vernier machine (HTS-DSSLVM) and its performance is compared with recently developed DSSLVM.

articleTitle: Contactless piston position transducer with axial excitation
abstract: Pneumatic cylinders for precise applications usually have integrated piston position sensors for fine control. In this paper we suggest new AC piston position transducer using axial coil directly wound on the cylinder surface as a field source.

articleTitle: Design of a novel high-torque-density in-wheel switched reluctance motor for electric vehicles
abstract: In-wheel switched reluctance motors (SRMs) have been applied to electric vehicles (EVs) for direct drive to eliminate the transmission loss, due to its feature of low cost, fault tolerance, wide speed range, simple and robust structure [1-2]. A novel multiple teeth topology of SRMs combining the feature of higher number of rotor poles and two teeth per stator pole is presented. The structure of two teeth can improve the output torque. Increasing the number of rotor poles results in larger slot area for winding and allows larger excitation current. The analysis and calculation are done by FEM and the motor is optimized by using GA. The results of the theoretical analysis and FEM simulation demonstrate that the proposed topology has higher torque output and less torque ripple. Moreover, the specific torque can be improved greatly. Therefore, the proposed topology may have good prospects for the application to EVs.

articleTitle: Study on electromagnetic force characteristics acting on levitation/guidance coils of a superconducting Maglev vehicle system
abstract: Superconducting Maglev has been developed as a high-speed transport system. The aim of the study of the authors is to establish an improved method to design the vehicle system with the objective of not only optimization of characteristics of the vehicle, but also consideration of durability of LG coils. As preliminary studies to establish the improved method, characteristics of electromagnetic forces acting on LG coils with respect to the parameters of the vehicle are being studied by computer simulations.

articleTitle: Flux weakening performance of permanent magnet synchronous motors with a conical rotor
abstract: Since electric vehicle drive system has high requirements, traction motors should be design and controlled with high output power performance throughout the entire driving range as well as with high torque performance at low speed range.

articleTitle: Experimental evaluation of the static characteristics of multi-degree-of-freedom spherical actuators
abstract: Multi-degree-of-freedom (multi-DOF) actuators have been developed for the fields of robotics and industrial machinery.In general, the actuating system with several degrees of freedom is composed of single-DOF motors, which results in large, heavy and complicated structures. Therefore, multi-DOF actuators are expected to solve these problems, and various types of actuators have been studied. Unlike 1-DOF motors, the multi-DOF actuators can generate torques in various positions and directions. Due to this, it is difficult to measure the static torque characteristics. In this paper, in order to experimentally evaluate the static characteristics of a multi-DOF actuator, its flux linkage is firstly measured using a 3-RRR parallel mechanism, and its torque constant map is calculated. The static torque characteristics are evaluated using the torque constant map. Finally, the effectiveness of this method is discussed.

articleTitle: Energy-encrypted contactless charging for swarm robots
abstract: As one emerging bionic technique, the swarm robotics is a coordination and control strategy of multiple-robot systems, where a number of relatively simple robots are effectively integrated to complete sophisticated tasks while possessing characteristics of high robustness, flexibility, and low cost.Alike other electrified devices, however, the energy storage is an inevitable technique issue impeding the development of swarm robotics. Instead of improving battery technology, the wireless power transfer (WPT) can make robots harness the energy in a cordless way and then charge their batteries even in the moving situation, thus fundamentally solving the problems of short working time due to the limited battery storage. In order to fulfill the selective energy transmission mechanism and then improve the charging performance, this paper proposes an energy-encrypted contactless charging system for swarm robots.

articleTitle: When does magnetostriction not conserve volume?
abstract: Magnetostriction is the strain associated with collective magnetic order. An iron bar expands slightly in the direction of magnetization when it is saturated in a magnetic field applied along its length, but when the experiment is conducted in a liquid, confined so that, when displaced, it can only expand along a narrow glass tube, no net change of volume is observed. The expansion of the iron in the direction of the applied field is compensated by a contraction half as large in the two perpendicular directions. This volume-conserving effect is named `Joulian magnetostriction'. A recent claim that the giant magnetostriction of 200-300 ppm in Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">100-x</sub>Ga<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> alloys with x = 17 or 26, known as Galfenol, was largely non-Joulian prompted us to re-evaluate the magnetically-induced strain in crystals of this material. Although we were unable to confirm the claim, we gained some insight into circumstances when magnetoelastic effects do not conserve volume, which is the subject of this contribution, in which we consider spontaneous volume magnetostriction.

articleTitle: The new multiferroic composite materials consisted of ferromagnetic, ferroelectric and polymer components
abstract: The multiferroic materials are of great interest now. Magnetoelectric effect in multiferroic composites consisted of ferroelectric and ferromagnetic components is the result of mechanical connection between components and magnetostriction and piezoelectric effects. The multilayer multiferroic composites are studied mostly.

articleTitle: Magnetic properties of L10 FeNi phase developed through annealing of an amorphous alloy
abstract: Demand for permanent magnets is increasing. We obtained L1<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> FeNi phase in different alloy systems. The types of phases formed depend on thermal treatment and elements present in the amorphous state. For example, in FeNiSiBPCu, the possible magnetic phases can be fcc FeNi, L1<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> FeNi, bcc-Fe and iron-borides.

articleTitle: High frequency magnetic thin film inductor integrated on flexible organic substrates
abstract: The increasing trend of electronics systems in diverse conventional and unconventional usage, especially propelled by the applications in mobile devices and internet of things (IoTs), has driven the miniaturization of various functionalities and circuitry on chip, including normally off-chip, bulky passive elements such as inductors.

articleTitle: A model to compute the resonance effects in high current instrument transformers
abstract: High current instrument transformers (HCTs) are widely used to measure high currents (5 kA and more) in power plants, power grids and special high current applications.These devices are usually designed for operation at power frequency (e. g. 50 Hz or 60 Hz) and have to have a high accuracy (1 % or better). Regarding standard [1], the accuracy of HCTs has to maintain even when using different burden. Due to the rising number of power electronic devices, the amount of harmonic currents in the power grid increases and shall be measured by HCTs, too. These harmonic currents as well as transient currents may cause resonance effects inside HCTs, which results in high measuring errors in thethe affected frequency range [2]. Furthermore, these resonances cause high voltages at the secondary side of the HCT, which may endanger persons and the installed equipment. To estimate and consider resonance effects during the design phase of HCTs, a model is developed to compute the resonance effects of a HCT only by using its production data.

articleTitle: A high force density HTS tubular vernier machine
abstract: In low speed direct drive applications, conventional permanent magnet synchronous machines (PMSM) suffer from bulky size due to large number of winding pole pairs.

articleTitle: Iron-loss characteristics using a 1MHz GaNFET PWM inverter
abstract: Next-Generation semiconductor devices like Silicon Carbide (SiC) or Gallium Nitride (GaN) have been introduced for many applications in power electronics due to their outstanding characteristics of high frequency and low loss operation [1].

articleTitle: Voltage-controlled magnetic tunnel junction based MRAM for replacing high density DRAM circuits corresponding to 2X nm generation
abstract: This work deeply investigated the feasibility of VC-MTJ based main memory and clarified its requirements to VC-MTJ for the first time. In this investigation, “high-speed read” for DRAM is as feasible as VC-MTJ for cache memory.

articleTitle: Effect of rotor geometry on Peak and Average Torque of direct drive External-Rotor Synchronous Reluctance Motor (Ex-R SynRM) in comparison with Switched Reluctance Motor for low speed domestic application
abstract: This paper deals with the feasibility of developing an External-Rotor Synchronous Reluctance Motor for a low speed direct drive domestic application. Here, an attempt is made to identify the rotor geometry which provides high peak, average torque and saliency ratio in comparison with the equivalent External-Rotor Switched Reluctance Motor which is developed and tested already for the same application. In this context, 6 different rotor geometries are considered for the feasibility study and performance characteristics are predicted using finite element analysis. These results are compared with equivalent size Ex-R SRM and finally, a feasible rotor geometry is proposed for further investigation and prototype.

articleTitle: Development of STT-MRAM for embedded memory applications
abstract: Spin Transfer Torque Magnetic Random Access Memory (STT-MRAM) is a leading candidate for embedded memory applications, with promises of low power, high performance, and non-volatility.

articleTitle: In-plane magnetic anisotropy detection for crystal grain orientation in Goss-textured ferromagnets
abstract: The quality of Goss-textured ferromagnets is expressed in terms of the orientation of its crystal grains. The best performance of cubic crystal grain magnetic materials, such as the electrical steels, is ideally realized when each grain is oriented according to the Goss orientation. In real materials the grains are not perfectly aligned and this reduces strongly their performances.

articleTitle: New single phase flux switching axial flux permanent magnet motor
abstract: Conventional single phase permanent magnet (PM) brushless DC motors (BLDC) are used in low power consumption applications, which require relatively small torque, such as fans and pumps. In this paper, a new topology of a single phase FSPM is proposed. In the final paper, a detailed characteristic analysis will be carried out, by varying the rotor teeth pole pitch, the chamfer depth and length, the stator slot opening width and also increasing the number of rotor poles and stator slots.

articleTitle: Improved figure-of-eight coil for transcranial magnetic stimulation using magnetic resonant coupling
abstract: Due to the significant morbidity and mortality, psychiatric disorders have been recognized as a worldwide public health issue.

articleTitle: Elman neural network-based identification of Krasnosel'skii-Pokrovskii model for magnetic shape memory alloys actuator
abstract: Magnetic shape memory alloys (MSMA), which are a class of innovative functional materials and possess a large strain and high response frequency, are used as the actuators to be applied widely in high-precision positioning, such as optical alignments, diamond turning machines and scanning probe microscopy.

articleTitle: Crystal orientation dependence of magnetization and magnetostriction behaviors in highly textured Galfenol and Alfenol thin sheets
abstract: Fe-Ga (Galfenol) and Fe-Al (Alfenol) single crystal alloys exhibit peak magnetostriction values along <;100> and have low magnetocrystalline anisotropy with positive sign (K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>=~10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> J/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>) at ~20 at.

articleTitle: Detection of inter-turn stator faults in induction motors using short term averaging of forwards and backwards rotating stator current phasors for fast prognostics
abstract: There are several methods for detecting shorted turns in the stators of induction motors.

articleTitle: Influence of inductance properties on a magnetic levitation for thin steel plates
abstract: In the steel industry, the demand for thin steel plates having beneficial functions obtained by surface processing increases rapidly. Then, the requirements to surface-qualities of the steel plates are becoming stricter. Accordingly, we are sure that magnetic levitation technique is best to deal with such functional steel plates, because nothing touches the surfaces of steel plate while treating it. We have already studied the steel plate's elasticity and vibrations and successfully carried out many experiments on magnetic levitation for the steel plates so far. (Refer to [1] - [3]). However, it is a serious problem for us how we determine the inductance value of a very thin steel plate in designing an optimal controller for levitating the plate. This paper shows the properties of “leakage inductance” and “magnetic saturation” between an electromagnet and a very thin steel plate based on many measurements, and with these properties, we verify the stability of an optimally controlled magnetic levitation system by means of “pole arrangements”.

articleTitle: Analysis of low-speed IPMMs with distributed and fractional slot concentrated windings designed for wind energy applications
abstract: This research studies the design of an interior permanent magnet synchronous machine (IPMM) for direct-drive wind energy applications. Minimum cogging torque, torque ripple, and maximum efficiency are amongst the priority design goals in this design optimization process. Special focus is given on the electromagnetic design, parameter optimization that is essential for wind turbine (WT) application. The winding layout is analyzed and both the distributed and concentrated wound IPMMs are compared for adaptable design optimization. This paper demonstrates the superiority of a concentrated-wound design and constructs a prototype machine based on the proposed design for experimental verification. The application of FSCW PM machine in wind turbines is a fairly new concept with very limited literature (that too only using finite element analysis methods) available that specifies the use of PM machines with FSCW stator for wind applications. The features known for an optimal design of a D-D PM wind turbine generator includes the generator's mass, efficiency, load torque ripple, no-load cogging torque and manufacturing costs [1]. According to [2, 3], the cogging torque should ideally be limited between 1.5% and 2% of the rated torque for the efficient functioning of WTs. The main aim of this research is to build a prototype IPMM suitable for low-speed applications based on extensive electromagnetic FEA analysis. The initial part of this paper aims to determine the correct geometry and winding structure based on its set of design goals. Cogging torque and torque ripple minimization techniques are discussed based on parametric optimization of the rotor and stator. The final prototype design and its experimental verification are also presented to verify the FEA results.

articleTitle: Design and optimization of a novel linear flux-reversal permanent magnet machines with large mover slot opening
abstract: A novel LFRPM with consequent-poles and large mover slot opening is proposed in this paper. The cost of PMs of the proposed machine is only a quarter of the conventional LFRPM and the average thrust can be improved by 51 % compared to the conventional machine. The thrust ripple of the proposed machine is reduced to less than 2% with the combination of three-sectional structure and mover slot-skewing. The performance of the proposed machine is calculated by FEM and the results verify the superiority of the proposed machine.

articleTitle: A low cost magnetically geared lead screw
abstract: Electromagnetic linear actuator (ELAs) have the advantage over hydraulic and mechanical mechanisms of being able to operate with higher efficiencies and are potentially more reliable.

articleTitle: Battery-less Hall sensor operated by energy harvesting from a single Wiegand pulse
abstract: We operated a Hall sensor using energy harvesting from a magnetic wire.

articleTitle: Cost-effective vernier permanent-magnet machine with high torque performance
abstract: As a promising candidate applied in direct-drive applications due to high torque characteristics at low speed, vernier permanent-magnet (VPM) machines have been paid increasingly attention in many direct-drive fields, such as electric vehicle propulsion and wind power generation. In order to reduce the flux leakage and improve PM utilization rate on the premise of not decreasing the output torque, a five-phase fault-tolerant VPM machine is proposed with unipolar ferrite material between FMPs and surface mounted unipolar NdFeB in rotor, which not only remains the advantage of fault tolerance, but also significantly improves the torque density and reduce torque ripple simultaneously with considerable less consumption of rare-earth PM material.

articleTitle: Spin-orbit torque MRAM read reliability
abstract: In this paper, we present a precise read disturb mode in spin-orbit-torque (SOT)-MRAM. A precise model of read reliability was derived, and the model and simulation results confirmed that SOT-MRAM has a tradeoff between read and write performance. Furthermore, the stabilizing memory cell construction was proposed and applied to improve read reliability quantitatively.

articleTitle: Current harmonics of a current superimposition variable flux reluctance motor
abstract: Traction motors for electric vehicles and hybrid electric vehicles require wide power band characteristics. In order to increase the power band, field weakening control is widely used in interior permanent magnet motors. However, the effectiveness of the field weakening control is not sufficient for use in traction motors for vehicles. In addition, the motor efficiency is decreased due to the d-axis current. In order to solve the problem, we have developed a current superimposition variable flux reluctance motor (CSVFRM) in this paper.

articleTitle: Consolidation of magnetostrictive (001)-oriented Fe-Ga flakes for 3D printing powder materials
abstract: density. In this work, we investigate consolidation of Fe-Ga alloy flakes with varying particle size and demonstrate 3D printed Fe-Ga discs to evaluate their potential to transform commercial production. Flake-type particles were produced from ingots of Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">80</sub>Ga<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</sub> and Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">73</sub>Ga<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">27</sub> alloy by high-energy ball milling using a SPEX 8000 Mixer/Mill. Wet ball milling with isopropyl alcohol was employed to avoid shattering alloy pieces into irregular powders, which occurs during dry milling.

articleTitle: Enhanced coercivity of spark plasma sintered (La,Ce)FeB magnets
abstract: The increasing global demand on Nd-Fe-B makes rare earth (Re) elements including Nd, and Tb facing long-term criticality due to resource limitation and price, it is important to develop new Re-Fe-B magnets with high content of light rare earths (LRe) such as La and Ce which are more abundant and cheaper. However, large amounts exceeds 40 wt.% of La/Ce substitutions for Nd or Pr worse the properties. In addition, the nonmagnetic CeFe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> phase, which coexists with the main 2:14:1 phase, lowers the intrinsic magnetic properties of La/Ce-FeB. It is reported that the substitution of La for Ce can inhibit the formation of CeFe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and improve the magnetic properties of CeFeB magnets. In this study, we prepared a series of (La/Ce)FeB ribbons and investigated the effect of La content on the structure and magnetic properties. Based on the optimized (La/Ce)FeB ribbon, spark plasma sintered (SPS) nanocrystalline bulks with high density were fabricated, and (La/Ce)FeB magnets with NdCu additions, to improve the coercivity, were also investigated.

articleTitle: Micromagnetic model analysis of various spin torque oscillators with write head for microwave-assisted magnetic recording
abstract: Stable oscillation is one of the most important factors for spin-torque oscillators (STO) used in microwave-assisted magnetic recording (MAMR) [1].

articleTitle: An electromagnet-assisted ferrite magnet motor
abstract: EV/HEV traction motors are required to have contradictory characteristics such as high torque at low speeds and low torque at high speeds. To meet this requirement, our research group is studying a synchronous motor with a new structure.This paper proposes an electromagnet-assisted ferrite magnet motor (EMaFM) with a double-gap structure which generates the torque by using both ferrite magnets and electromagnets. The proposed EMaFM has the field regulation capability while utilizing the ferrite magnets.magnets. To validate its operating principle, a prototype machine is designed and manufactured. In addition, the electromagnetic performance of the prototype machine is simulated using finite element analysis (FEA) and is supported by experiments.

articleTitle: High temperature characterization of electrical steels using an adapted Epstein frame
abstract: The development of every electromagnetic devices requires the use of magnetic material to drive the magnetic flux.

articleTitle: Demagnetization fault detection for PMSM based marine propulsion motors using search coils in the stator slots
abstract: A marine electrical power system's fate in terms of its quality and maintenance heavily relies on the efficiency of its fault detection. This research develops an online approach to detecting demagnetization faults in a surface-mounted permanent magnet synchronous motor (SPMM) in a marine propulsion setting. The proposed methodology uses search coils to determine faults that reveal data to pinpoint which slot/magnet is affected by the faults, segregating fault symptoms from other asymmetric problems. This paper is distinctive in its acute detection of faults even when the severity of the fault is very minimal. The proposed model used for simulation in two-dimensional 2-D FEA is a 3-phase, 42 poles, 54 slots SPMM. The FEA results reveal the potential for proposed method to provide reliable data on fault diagnosis of marine propulsion motors.

articleTitle: Layer thickness effects and microstructure of CPP-GMR spin-valves with Ag/InZnO/Zn conductive oxide-based spacer layers
abstract: Improving the output of current-perpendicular-to-plane giant magnetoresistance (CPP-GMR) sensor has been the central issue to meet the requirements for next generation read sensors.sensors. Many works have demonstrated that ferromagnetic Co-based Heusler alloy films effectively enhance the CPP-GMR outputs because of the high spin-polarization of the Heusler alloys. In addition to the ferromagnetic layers, the material for the non-magnetic spacer layer also has a significant influence on the CPP-GMR output. Nakatani et al. recently reported that conductive oxides such as InZnO (IZO) could be used for spacer layer of CPP-GMR sensors. A relatively high magnetoresistance ratio (ΔR/R) of ~26% at resistance-area product (RA) ~0.1 Ω μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, which is in the suitable RA rangee for the read sensor application, was reported using Ag/IZO/Zn trilayer spacer for poly-crystalline spin-valve sensors. However, the mechanism of the improved ΔR/R at RA ~0.1 Ω μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> by the Ag/IZO/Zn spacer layer is unclear. In this work, we studied the effect of the layer thickness of the Ag/IZO/Zn trilayer spacer on RA and ΔR/R and the microstructure of the CPP-GMR sensors.

articleTitle: Characteristic analysis of surface permanent magnet vernier motor with concentrated winding according to pole ratio and winding pole number
abstract: In this research, various combinations of the rotor pole pairs and stator teeth of the SPMVM were investigated using 2-D FEM and their characteristics such as cogging torque, torque ripple and N-T characteristics were compared. In the full paper, the operational principle of the SPMVM will be described concretely and more characteristics such as a current versus torque and efficiency will be compared. Finally, the characteristics variation due to combinations of pole ratio of rotor magnet pole pairs and stator tooth will be described.

articleTitle: Influence of Magnetic slot Wedge Defect on Starting Performance of high voltage line-start permanent magnet synchronous motor
abstract: In the actual operation, the stator magnetic slot wedge is vibrated by the large alternating electromagnetic force, which causes the stator magnetic slot wedge to defect and then affect the starting performance and efficiency of motor.

articleTitle: Magnetic field analysis for dimensional resonance in Mn-Zn ferrite core and comparison with permeability measurement
abstract: Mn-Zn ferrite is widely used for inductors and transformers because of its high permeability and low loss in the low-frequency band. In this study, we attempted to perform the magnetic field simulation which is composed of the equivalent circuit and Maxwell equation for simulating both of the dimensional resonance and size-dependent core loss of Mn-Zn ferrite. By invocation of the equivalent circuit of Ref. [3], we used the relation between the current density and electric field with a dielectric effect of crystalline grain boundary. These equations are solved by coupling with Maxwell equation and magnetic property equation. To verify the effectiveness of the coupling analysis, we analyzed the frequency dependence of the permeability and the loss of several toroidal cores of different sizes as the first step.

articleTitle: Vector magnetic characteristics of Ultra-Thin Electrical Steel Sheet for development of high efficiency high speed motor
abstract: Recent years, developments of high speed motors are required to make high power and small size machines. In this paper, we will report the magnetic characteristics of ultrathin electrical steel sheet. Fig.1 (a) shows the results of measurements on initial magnetization curve of several types of soft magnetic materials. Conventional materials having excellent frequency characteristics show low magnetic permeability or low saturation magnetic flux density. The characteristic of Ultrathin electrical steel sheet is almost equal to NO (35A300) under exciting frequency of 50Hz. Fig.1 (b) shows the frequency characteristic of the Ultrathin electrical steel sheet. The eddy current loss is small than NO because thickness of this sheet is very thin (0.08 mm). Fig.1 (c) shows the (110) pole figure of ultrathin electrical steel sheet. It is confirmed that the roll induced magnetic anisotropy of this sheet is small. Fig.2 shows the laminated core for motor made of the ultrathin electrical steel sheet. By using this sheet to the cores of high speed motors, downsizing, high efficiency and high output can be expected. In the full version of papers, the vector magnetic characteristic and magnetic power loss under various conditions are examined in more detail.

articleTitle: Study of a linear Halbach passive magnetic damper
abstract: High voltage ultra-fast circuit breakers are operated with fast actuators. They are capable of generating impulsive force to swiftly open electrical contacts in a couple of milliseconds. Opening of the contacts with high velocities implies a need for a timely and controllable damping. An efficient damping mechanism then is crucial to attain an appropriate actuation performance and secure a long lifetime. In this paper a finite element model of a Halbach magnet array based magnetic damper and a corresponding experimental prototype is described. It was found that a uniform and high radial component of the magnetic flux density is necessary in order to achieve high damping force. The radial magnetic field can be controlled via thickness and magnetization direction of the ring magnets which are used to create the Halbach magnet array. Finally, it is also shown that the concept provides a frictionless collision free damping demonstrating its potential to be used in fast circuit breakers.

articleTitle: Effects of organic coating on hyperthermic efficiencies
abstract: Magnetic heating is based on the thermal energy generation via magnetic nanoparticle (MNP) mediators activated by alternating magnetic (AC) field.

articleTitle: Experimental verification on effects in an emergency stop by installation of magneto rheological fluid damper to an elevator
abstract: In the countries sailing with an economic tailwind, many skyscrapers are going up.In this paper, we would like to confirm the real effects of our new structure by some experiments with test installation which is composed of an MRF damper, a spring, an elevator cage, linear servo mechanics with a ball screw for generating the brake force of E.S.D., sensors and a digital controller with Labview.

articleTitle: Temperature scaling of anisotropy field in HAMR recording
abstract: Currently, heat assisted magnetic recording (HAMR) is the leading technology candidate to further increase areal density in magnetic recording. In HAMR, the recording medium is temporarily heated with a near field transducer that is energized by a laser to temperatures well above the Curie temperature Tc. Upon cooling, the magnetization is frozen in, where its direction is determined by the direction of the applied field. To accurately predict the quality of the recording, the temperature dependences of the anisotropy and magnetization near the Curie point have to be known.

articleTitle: On the design and construction assessments of a permanent magnet assisted synchronous reluctance motor
abstract: By appropriately inserting ferrite magnets into the rotor of a synchronous reluctance motor (SynRM), it is realized that the operational power factors and torque outputs of this SynRM can be improved. This paper will provide an evaluation index that can characterize the performance of PMA-SynRMs with different PM volume compositions, along with the impact assessments of the SynRMs with modified flux barriers obtained from thorough three-dimensional (3D) finite element analyses (FEA), a 3-hp PMA-SynRM will be constructed and the related experimental measurements will also be supported to validate the design arrangements.

articleTitle: Common-mode voltage supression of dual Y shift 30° six-phase electric machine
abstract: There are two common-mode voltages (CMVs) in a system composed of dual Y shift 30° six-phase electric machine and power converter, which bring detrimental effects on the system. To suppress the amplitude and changing frequency of CMV, a method with six-phase space vector pulse width modulation (SVPWM) is presented. The six intermediate vectors which become zero vectors in o1-o2 and z1-z2 planes are structured by twelve non-zero basic vectors with linear combination method. The two CMVs of each of these twelve basic vectors are equal. The expected vector in d-q plane can be synthesized by intermediate vectors. Experimental results show that the peak-to-peak value of CMV is 1/3 of DC-bus voltage of converter, the changing frequency of CMV is much less than the switching frequency of converter.

articleTitle: A room-temperature resettable thermomagnetic-piezoelectric MEMS magnetic sensor
abstract: Recently, the magnetoelectric sensors have been studied because these sensors have great potential to sense ultralow magnetic field [1–2].

articleTitle: Optimal design of an inset PM motor with assisted barriers and magnet shifting for improvement of torque characteristics
abstract: Inset permanent magnet (PM) synchronous motor (PMSM) has been widely used in various occasions due to its high efficiency and high torque density, such as the electric vehicle, wind power generation, ship propulsion, home appliances and other high precision machining and servo control systems [1]-[3]. This paper introduces a way of magnet shifting and assisted barriers into an inset motor. Then, the proposed inset PM motor can guarantee the torque density with great reduction of on-load torque ripple because the assisted barriers can not only enhance the utilization of reluctance torque but also will not introduce any other torque harmonic and even can further reduce torque ripple.

articleTitle: Development of reliable gearless motors for electric vehicles
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) are the cleanest and greenest road transportation for smart cities [1].The purpose of this paper is to design and analyze a new class of reliable gearless motors for EVs based on the MagD concept. Namely, the magnetic steering (MS) winding is incorporated into the single-stator double-rotor stator-field motor to realize the MagD for EVs. While the stator-field motor has different topologies and the generalization includes both radial-field (RF) and axial-field (AF) morphologies, the flux-switching DC (FSDC) topology has the merits of high robustness, low material cost and flexible field control [5] and the AF morphology has the advantages of high torque density and high power density.

articleTitle: Direct functionalization of magnetic hollow spheres with (3-aminopropyl)triethoxysilane (APTES) for targeted drug delivery
abstract: Direct functionalization strategy has been employed to modify the surface of the magnetic hollow spheres with (3-Aminopropyl)triethoxysilane (APTES) for targeted drug delivery. Magnetic hollow spheres were characterized by XRD, BET, FE-SEM, VSM and FT-IR. Model drug camptothecin (CPT) has been used to evaluate drug loading and in vitro release.

articleTitle: Magnetoresistive sensor with high sensitivity: Self-aligned magnetic structures
abstract: Summary form only given. To accomplish the task, we propose the magnetoresistive structure in which the magnetic layer occurs under the sloped conductors and repeats their shape. This structure may be called self-aligned. Mathematical simulation shown that with using a self-aligned structure the sensitivity of AMR converter increases without changing other geometric dimensions. There is an optimum size of the protrusion height (3 μm), which allows to maximize the sensitivity and prevent the occurrence of hysteresis (6 μm). To confirm the results of the simulation a test batch AMR converters with self-combined structure was made. The measurement results have confirmed an increase in sensitivity while maintaining the geometric dimensions. AMR effect in permalloy film in the produced batch was 2.5 %. The coercive force and anisotropy field reached 1.8 Oe and 5 Oe, respectively. It should be mentioned that this effect is lower for structures with wider magnetic stripe.

articleTitle: Spin-valve junction with transfer-free MoS2 spacer prepared by sputtering
abstract: The prospect of spintronic devices based on two-dimensional metal dichalcogenide material (2DMX<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) originate from their long spin life time and 100% out-of-plane spin polarization. Here we report the fabrication of LSMO/MoS<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>/NiFe spin valve structure. 2nm MoS<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> layer on LSMO electrode was grown by RF sputtering. Because of high vapor pressure of sulfide, MoS<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> was deposited at room temperature to prevent vaporization of sulfide and followed by 450°C post annealing process under a nitrogen atmosphere at 1 atm. The Raman spectroscopy measurement of MoS<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> sputter deposited on Si and LSMO/STO substrates are shown in Fig. 1. The Raman spectrum shows E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2g</sub> and A<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1g</sub> vibration modes of MoS<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, suggesting that crystalline MoS<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> layer is successfully grown on different substrates. The top permalloy electrode was deposit by e-beam evaporation to prevent damages of MoS<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> layer. Negative magnetoresistance effect is observed under 20 K with an MR% up to 0.8%. The results suggest a new method to fabricate 2DMX<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> spintronic and electronic devices with a transfer-free process for obtaining reliable contacts.

articleTitle: 4-sensor yokeless electric current transducer
abstract: Contactless transducers of DC electric currents often have magnetic yoke which concentrates the flux generated by the measured current. As a result, the reading does not depend much on the conductor position inside the magnetic circuit. The yoke also shields against external magnetic fields including those caused by external currents (crosstalk error).

articleTitle: Improving BER performance by using V-shaped read head array in heat assisted magnetic recording
abstract: As the micromagnetic simulations are computationally demanding, we propose a fast and simplified write model to capture the transition curvature of HAMR. As the transition curvatures cause signal degradation in normally oriented read head array (NHA) having straight gaps, hence we propose a V-shaped read head array (VHA) by rotating the side readers at appropriate angles to follow the curvature shapes and improve the readback signal. For the simplified write channel model in HAMR, the recording field is assumed as 10.5 kOe and spatially uniform with a 45° angle relative to the perpendicular axis, corresponding to an effective field H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</sub> of 21 kOe with Stoner-Wohlfarth model.

articleTitle: Power loss and demagnetization research for high speed permanent magnet electrical machine
abstract: High speed permanent magnet machines (HSPMMs) have earned extensive interests in industrial application such as compressors, centrifuges and pumps due to their dramatic advantages of high power density, high efficiency and compact size [1-2]. However, high rotating speed and small size also brings challenge, as high frequency magnetic field induces large power loss density, and thermal dissipation condition becomes poorer with the compact size. In this paper, a MW rate, 18000 rpm HSPMM for compressor application is designed and researched by Finite element method (FEM). It is a 27 slots, 4 pole machine structure with high strength carbon fiber sleeve applied around the surface-mounted PM poles for mechanical integrity during high speed rotation.

articleTitle: A novel linear machine with amorphous primary core
abstract: This paper proposes a novel DC-excited flux-modulated linear machine with new primary structure for utilizing amorphous core. Although amorphous core is regarded as a good candidate in high efficient electric machine, and being investigated for decades, it has not been widely used in electric machines yet. The key problem is the difficulty in slotting. For the new structure, the difficulty in slotting is avoided. Furthermore, the proposed machine is economical and has robust double salient structure without any permanent magnets (PMs), and both the field winding and the armature winding are located together in the primary core. In addition, both windings are single-toothed. By regulating the field excitation, the machine can operate at a wide speed range. Due to the low loss of amorphous core, this machine shows high efficiency at high speed.

articleTitle: A study on relationship between recording pattern and decoding reliability in SMR
abstract: Hard disk drives (HDDs) have played the central role as the information storage system. HDDs of much larger capacity are needed in highly networked information society. To meet the requirement, two-dimensional magnetic recording (TDMR) using a shingled magnetic recording (SMR) is studied. In this study, we investigate the relationship between the recording pattern and the decoding reliability by classifying the log-likelihood ratio (LLR) at the a posteriori probability (APP) decoder output according to the recording patterns under an SMR R/W channel specification of 4 Tbit/inch<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> by computer simulation.

articleTitle: An improved equivalent magnetic circuit model of coreless axial flux permanent magnet synchronous machine
abstract: An axial flux permanent magnet synchronous machine (AFPMSM) with double external rotors and coreless internal stator can operate at higher efficiency without the stator core losses and cogging torque.

articleTitle: Optimal design of saturated switched reluctance machine for low torque ripple and high average torque
abstract: A switched reluctance motor has been one of possible candidates of rare-earth-free-motors. This paper focuses on the optimal design method of switched reluctance machines (SRMs) for mitigating torque ripple and improving average torque under the low speed operation. In order to improve the startup performance of micro electric vehicles (EVs) and reduce the converter capacity, a SRM with four times overload torque is required.

articleTitle: First vs second order magnetocaloric material for thermomagnetic energy conversion
abstract: The supply of waste heat represents a huge and freely available amount of energy that make it a key target for energy conversion technologies, notwithstanding the small thermodynamic efficiency to be expected because of the limited working temperature difference.Energy harvesting systems from waste heat based on thermomagnetic generation (TMG) have been studied.

articleTitle: Rotor fault analysis in a doubly-fed induction generator using impedance matrix technique
abstract: Condition monitoring is a standard method for scheduling maintenance and ensuring that catastrophic failures do not occur in industrial motors.

articleTitle: Doubly salient dual-PM linear machines for regenerative shock absorbers
abstract: Regenerative shock absorbers (RSAs) can convert the kinetic energy originally dissipated in the dampers to electrical energy, with the help of electric machines [1, 2]. In this paper, a new class of linear machines, termed as the doubly salient dual-PM (DSDPM) linear machines, is proposed. The proposed DSDPM linear machine has PMs on both the stator and mover, so-called the dual-PM structure.

articleTitle: Iterative channel detection with LDPC product code for bit patterned media recording
abstract: Because of the explosion in data growth, the requirement for storage system with high density has been increased. Bit patterned media recording (BPMR) is a candidate for the next generation magnetic systems which has many advantages to achieve recording density of 1 Tb/in<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and beyond. This paper proposes an iterative channel detection scheme with low density parity check (LDPC) product code using extrinsic information between soft output Viterbi algorithm (SOVA) and LDPC for BPMR.

articleTitle: Torque ripple minimization of variable flux reluctance machines by rotor skewing
abstract: Variable flux reluctance machines (VFRM) are an interesting candidate to substitute permanent-magnet synchronous machines in many applications, mainly owing to the absence of rare-earth permanent magnets and improved field weakening capability.

articleTitle: High perpendicular anisotropy in sub-30 nm MRAM devices measured by spin-torque ferromagnetic resonance
abstract: Spin Transfer Torque Magnetic Random Access Memory (STT-MRAM) is the leading technology for next generation non-volatile embedded memories. In this presentation, we use Spin-Torque Ferromagnetic Resonance (ST-FMR) to measure the anisotropy field of perpendicularly magnetized devices down to 25 nm in size. We show that the effective anisotropy field HK<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</sub>, including the demagnetizing field, exceeds 10 kOe at room temperature. The corresponding interfacial anisotropy field is close to 20 kOe. The magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ) stack used in this work consists of perpendicularly magnetized CoFeB-based magnetic electrodes separated by a MgO tunnel barrier. The reference layer (RL) is made out of a synthetic antiferromagnet (SAF) so as to minimize the dipolar field on the free layer (FL).

articleTitle: A novel linear permanent magnet vernier machine with consequent poles and Halbach permanent magnet array
abstract: Linear permanent magnet vernier machine (LPMVM) has the feature of high thrust density at low speed, which make it a suitable solution for direct-drive applications [1], such as pumps and linear servo system.

articleTitle: Dual freelayer reader for improved linear density
abstract: The Bottom Spin Valve (BSV) geometry has been the standard HDD Reader design for well over 10 years [1].

articleTitle: A proposal of an one-axis active control type bearingless motor integrating radial passive magnetic bearings and a thrust active magnetic bearing
abstract: A bearingless motor (BelM) integrating function of an electric motor and a magnetic bearing (MB) can generate torque while magnetically suspending rotor shaft without mechanical contact.

articleTitle: Direct torque control of open winding brushless doubly-fed machine
abstract: The BDFM is developed by the cascade induction machine. In recent years, the research on the control method of BDFM has made remarkable progress. There are mainly two kinds of control methods are used for BDFM, that is, the field oriented control(FOC) and direct torque control(DTC). Compared with FOC, DTC does not need the complex coordinate transformation, the control system is simple and reliable and the robustness of the system is improved. In this paper, in order to solve the problem of low precision of traditional DTC for BDFM, open winding of BDFM is adopted based on the twelve-section partition. The open winding BDFM model is established through the simulation and the result compared with that of the not open winding shows that the torque ripple is reduced and the stator flux waveforms are more smooth.

articleTitle: Distributed parameter model for electromagnetic valve actuator with permanent magnet
abstract: Permanent magnet (PM) and soft magnetic materials in electromagnetic equipment has been widely used in industrial product [1–3].

articleTitle: A miniaturized force sensor based on hair-like flexible magnetized cylinders deposited over a giant magnetoresistive sensor
abstract: The detection of low-magnitude forces (under 1mN) is essential in applications that require either a very high sensitivity and resolution acquisition (e.g. detection of microfluidic flows) or very high reliability and control (e.g. biomedical or humanoid robotics). In this work, we present a bio-inspired ciliary force sensor consisting in an array of magnetized, flexible quasi-elastic pillars deposited over a magnetoresistive GMR sensor. The GMR sensor stack (Ta 10/NiFe 28/CoFe 25/Cu 26/CoFe 23/MnIr 80/Ta 30, thickness in Å) was deposited at INESC-MN by ion beam and patterned in series array of 120 elements with 60 x 3 μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, over a total area of 3 x 3 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, resulting in a sensitivity of 22.5 Ω Oe<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>.

articleTitle: A new electro-magnetic brake for actuator locking mechanism in aerospace vehicle
abstract: Electro-magnetic brakes are gaining importance in aerospace vehicles for various critical applications. A new electro-magnetic brake is designed which is more efficient and reliable compared to conventional solenoid operated brake. The non-linear magnetic analysis is carried out on the brake and results are presented. The results are promising and this topology can be adapted for aerospace and other critical applications.

articleTitle: Voltage-tunable stochastic computing with magnetic bits
abstract: In this paper, we model and design spintronic circuits that exploit the inherent stochasticity of nanomagnetic dynamics, while providing ultra-low-energy (~ 3-5 aJ/bit) and ultra-low-power (<; 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) operation.

articleTitle: Magnetic flux analysis of a new Field Excitation Flux Switching Motor with segmental rotor
abstract: Since a few decade, Induction Machines (IMs) have been utilized in most of electrical appliances due to their low cost, simple circuit for starting and wide operating range [1].

articleTitle: Permanent magnet eddy current loss analysis of interior PM machines for electric vehicle application
abstract: This paper has analyzed and compared the PM eddy current loss of six interior PM machines for electric vehicle applications.

articleTitle: Design and analysis of a new HTS electromagnetic screw for artificial heart
abstract: Linear actuators provided thrust force and displacement for many applications.

articleTitle: Influence of end-effect on direct and quadrature inductances in linear electromagnetic actuators
abstract: Direct and quadrature inductances, L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</sub> and L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</sub>, respectively, are an essential property of motors and actuators that must be known in order to develop precise control systems for high performance applications.

articleTitle: Fabrication hard magnet by 3D printing
abstract: This study was aimed to utilize polymer compounding technology with polymer materials and hard magnetic powder to produce a polymer composite material that has a magnetic capability, and use 3D printing technology of FDM (Fused Deposition Modeling) technology to form the magnetic devices. In this experiment, the study is focused on how to improve the magnetic properties of polymer composite material and explore the influence of the magnetic material of overall solid content, and by adjusting the FDM molding conditions to improve the dense structure of printed object to achieve better magnetic properties.

articleTitle: Performance factor comparison of nanocrystalline, amorphous and crystalline soft magnetic materials for medium frequency applications
abstract: The efficiency of electromagnetic devices, such as e.g. transformers, is influenced by the losses of the applied soft magnetic material. Different structured materials are available but choosing the appropriate material is not instinctive. A performance factor is evaluated in this paper for frequencies up to 10 kHz. The studied application is a medium frequency transformer. A semi-physical iron loss model is used to describe the measured losses. These results are used to determine the performance factor for various boundary conditions.

articleTitle: Development of a new low cost transverse flux-flux switching permanent magnet machine with soft magnetic composite cores and ferrite magnets
abstract: Soft magnetic composite (SMC) material is a new soft magnetic material, now it is popular in the designing of permanent magnet machine where high operation frequency and 3-D flux path required, due to its advantages of low eddy current loss and magnetic isotropy.expensive. In this paper, based on the ferrite magnet and SMC cores, a new transverse flux flux switching permanent magnet machine (TFFSPMM) is proposed for the low cost application. The performance of the TFFSPMM is good as the usage of high flux concentrating ability of the new machine topology and the global winding.

articleTitle: Enhancement for high speed switching of Magneto-Optic Fiber-Based routing using single magnetizing coil
abstract: This paper introduces a new approach to enhance the efficiency and speed of magneto-optic (MO) switching systems that will allow faster possibilities in fiber based routing systems. The new design uses single coil configuration with newly designed circuit, that is capable of better optimization of the MO material's magnetization and demagnetization process.

articleTitle: A basic theory of induction heating for wind powered thermal energy system
abstract: Wind power is a widely-used renewable energy source, which requires power stabilization because of its intermittency. As Siemens recently announced the development of thermal energy storing system for wind power generation [1], heat is a cost-effective energy form for a largescale energy storage. We are developing a wind powered thermal energy system (WTES) that can convert the wind power efficiently into the thermal energy to be stored for a stable and low-cost electric power generation [2]. Our study showed that the induction heating can be the most efficient heat generation for the WTES, since it can realize very light and robust rotating machine. This article derives a basic formula of induction heating to reveal dominant factors for the conceptual design of WTES.

articleTitle: A new mover separated linear magnetic-field modulated motor for long stroke applications

articleTitle: Integrated motor propulsor magnet design with hybrid Halbach array for torque ripple reduction
abstract: Motivation for research Recently, integrated motor propulsors (IMPs) have been under extensive research and development because of the numerous advantages of underwater propulsion for vehicles, such as a simple, quiet, lightweight, and small-size structure. In this paper, the design and analysis of an IMP for a 30-hp 1,500-rpm-class unmanned submarine are presented. This paper is divided into two main parts: the PM width ratio optimization with torque ripple, the influence of the back-emf that changes according to the PM material. The first part focuses on the PM width ratio, which use a downscaled PM to compensate for the torque pulsation. Because the magnetization of a magnet in the x-axis direction is the same as that in the air gap, the torque ripple varies. The second part is based on the PM material. Generally, the same arrangement is used in the Halbach array, but the back-emf is affected by the magnet width in the y-axis direction. The material of radial array (magnetized in the x-axis direction) PM does not matter if the material cahges because x-axis does not significantly affect the magnetic flux. The results are calculated by a two-dimensional finite element method (FEM). In a future study, a more specific comparison with an accurate initial design method in consideration of the mechanical structure will be thoroughly investigated for its contribution to related researches and industrial applications.

articleTitle: Spin-current manipulation of photoinduced magnetization dynamics in Ta/CoFeB based nanostructures
abstract: Spin currents offer a way to control static and dynamic magnetic properties, and therefore they are crucial for next-generation MRAM devices or spin-torque oscillators. Manipulating the dynamics is especially interesting within the context of photo-magnonics. In typical 3d transition metal ferromagnets like CoFeB, the lifetime of light-induced magnetization dynamics is restricted to about 1 ns, which e.g. strongly limits the opportunities to exploit the wave nature in a magnonic crystal filtering device. Here, we report on the potential of spin-currents to increase the spin wave lifetime in a simple trilayer system, consisting of a heavy metal (8 nm of β-Tantalum (Platinum)), 5 nm CoFeB, capped by 3 nm Ruthenium. The samples were grown in UHV by magnetron sputtering (Ta, CoFeB) and E-beam evaporation (Pt, Ru), and subsequently patterned into micron-sized conduction strips using E-beam-lithography. Due to the spin Hall effect, the heavy metal layer generates a transverse spin current when a lateral charge current passes through the strip. Using time-resolved all-optical pump-probe spectroscopy, we investigate how this spin current affects the magnetization dynamics in the adjacent CoFeB layer. By analyzing the Kittel mode's frequency as a function of the charge current, we determine how Joule-heating affects the saturation magnetization. Furthermore, from extracting the current dependence of the effective Gilbert damping parameter, we have found Spin Hall angles of Θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Ta</sub> = -0.043(11) for Ta and Θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Pt</sub> = 0,086(12) for Pt. While such results can also be obtained from more established methods like BLS or ST-FMR, the benefit of our experimental approach lies in the possibility to investigate (sub-) picosecond dynamics. For instance, a look at the sub-picosecond timescale demonstrates that also the physics of ultrafast demagnetization can be manipulated by spin currents. The authors acknowledge financial support of the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft within CRC 1073.

articleTitle: Magnetic modelling of a Linear Synchronous Machine with Spectral Element Method
abstract: Reducing the computational effort for the machine models remains a priority for machine designers.Therefore, the Finite Element Analysis (FEA) needs replacing with faster models in optimisation routines. For some machines, these assumptions are not admissible. A new method for analysis of electrical machines is Spectral Element Method (SEM) which allows modelling of non-square subdomain geometries and at the same time maintain the spectral accuracy . The resulting system of equations will be less compared to FEA. To illustrate, a Linear Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine (LPMSM) geometry is modelled using SEM including the nonlinear material properties of the iron. The performance of the model is discussed and compared with FEA regarding absolute error and computational time.
