articleTitle: Arrays of bi-metal nanostructures to control energy product
abstract: Bi-metal magnetic nanostructures have been deposited within porous silicon to influence the magnetic switching behavior of the porous silicon/metal nanocomposite. These magnetic nanocomposites consisting of two ferromagnetic metals have been achieved by two different routes. On the one hand both metals have been deposited alternatingly out of one solution by changing the potential and on the other hand the two metals have been deposited by using different metal salt solutions. The latter system shows two distinct slopes of the hysteresis curves due to the different saturation behavior of the two types of deposited metal, whereas the system produced from one electrolyte shows no kink which indicates exchange coupling between the two metals. By tuning the amount of each metal the energy product of the systems can be controlled.

articleTitle: Effect of manganese on the microstructure and magnetic properties of Fe-Mn-Nb-B glassy ribbons
abstract: Metallic glasses (MGs) can be produced with a wide range of unique properties suiting them to a wide range of applications, from transformer cores to active elements inside sensors and other measurement devices.

articleTitle: Surface conditions on magnetic properties of Fe-based amorphous ribbon
abstract: Soft magnetic materials play an important role in electronic energy components such as inverter and converter using transformer, inductors, etc.

articleTitle: Design and analysis of double-rotors disc-type PM motor for contra-rotating propulsion system
abstract: Contra-rotating double-rotor disc-type PM motor is suitable to directly drive contra-rotating propeller of torpedo, due to avoid yawing and spinning. In this paper, the electromagnetic design scheme for different pole numbers are compared, and design method of permanent magnet size and stator winding are searched, then the effect of magnetic isolation material used in stator is analyzed. Finally, a prototype of 10.8kW 1000r/min is designed for performance analysis to verify the validity of theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstrations of unpinning domains in a saturated bismuth-substituted iron garnet
abstract: The utilization of a bismuth-substituted iron garnet as a magne-to-optic faraday rotator (MOFR) has been reported for all-optical networking purposes as well as for other applications [1 - 5]. When a significantly large magnetic field is applied to the MOFR, it will enter a saturated state. Once the material is saturated, the magnetic domains can become pinned into place [6]. In the past, unpinning the magnetic domains, and moving the MOFR material back into a desaturated state was a difficult task. This paper will present methods for unpinning the MOFR material, allowing the material to become desaturated.

articleTitle: Spin-orbit torques and spin Hall magnetoresistance in antiferromagnetic hexagonal ε-Mn3Ga/CoFeB bilayers
abstract: Here, we report on the spin-orbit effective fields and the spin Hall magnetoresistance in antiferromagnetic ε-Mn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Ga/CoFeB bilayers. Typical stacks, consist of c-plane Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>(0001) substrate/wedged-Mn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Ga(t)/CoFeB(1)/MgO(2)/Ta(1) (thicknesses in nanometer), are grown by magnetron sputtering at ambient temperature. The preferred hexagonal (0001) texture of the ε-Mn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Ga films is confirmed by the presence of the corresponding X-ray diffraction peak, measured on a thicker Mn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Ga sample. The films are patterned into micron-sized Hall bar devices for magnetotransport characterization. We focus on quantifying the spin Hall efficiency of ε-Mn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Ga/CoFeB bilayer ξ, while keeping in mind that the intrinsic spin Hall angle of ε-Mn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Ga is likely to be higher, due to imperfect spin transmission across the interface.

articleTitle: DC-biased high-power impedance measurement of planar magnetic cores up to 70 MHz
abstract: It is necessary to develop a measurement technology of planar magnetic cores at higher frequencies and higher power ranges to develop better power supply on chip (PwrSoc).

articleTitle: Mapping and estimating magnetic field variations due to a one-sided magnet
abstract: Homogeneous magnetic fields are desirable in nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) experiments for detecting the presence of nuclear species accurately. However, some applications such as oil well logging, perform NMR experiments in inhomogeneous magnetic fields with lower spatial accuracy. Achieving improvements in spatial features requires a better understanding of the field profiles in such inhomogeneous fields. Therefore, in this paper, the magnetic field variations introduced due to a one-sided magnet are simulated and studied. A magnetic and a non-magnetic object are placed in the near field of a permanent magnet. Sections of the magnet's near-field region depicting the field decay and variations along different directions are analyzed. Prior NMR measurements do indicate that minor field variations affect the response of the magnetic moments from region to region leading to undesirable peak broadening in the frequency spectrum. However, field variations can be advantageous if the magnetic field profile is pre-mapped and changes in field profiles by placing known nuclei are pre-estimated. Pre-estimation would lead to a improved understanding of spatial resolution. This technique would also be useful for medical imaging purposes where different methods are utilized to obtain improved spatial resolution and contrast between different tissues/matter.

articleTitle: A combinatorial approach to the study of Sm-Fe-Ti based 1∶12 hard magnetic films
abstract: High performance permanent magnets are key components in the development of more efficient electrical motors for electric and hybrid cars as well as gearless wind turbines.

articleTitle: Equilibrium magnetization states and hysteresis in ferromagnetic nanotubes with dipolar interacting spins
abstract: Magnetic nanostructures can be synthesized with different shapes such as disks, cylinders, rings and nanotubes Owing to their specific geometry and nanoscale size that have found distinctive applications due to their peculiar magnetic orderings.

articleTitle: Reduced q axis nonlinear MEC model for single layer IPM
abstract: Interior Permanent Magnet machine (IPM) has several advantages such as high power density and wide constant power speed ratio, therefore, it is very popular in electric and hybrid automotive industry. In this paper, a MEC of IPM is obtained including stator slots. In order to reduce MEC, a mathematical polynomial is used to represent the relationship between magnetomotive force (MMF) and flux. The polynomial is derived from the nonlinear magnetic behavior of the core material using machine geometry. Finally, nonlinear reluctances in the same flux path can be combined into an equation thus, the number of nonlinear equations and computation time are reduced.

articleTitle: Order of magnitude improvement of nano-contact spin torque nano-oscillator performance
abstract: Spin torque nano-oscillators (STNO) represent a unique class of nano-scale microwave signal generators where spin transfer torque (STT) from a direct spin-polarized current drives and controls the auto-oscillation of the local free layer magnetization, which through its oscillating magnetoresistance transforms the direct current into a tunable microwave voltage. In this study, we investigate the influence of the bottom Cu electrode thickness (t<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Cu</sub>) in nano-contact STNOs. All NC-STNOs were fabricated using dc magnetron sputtering from four different material stacks with the same general layer order Si/SiO2/ Pd(8)/Cu(t<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Cu</sub>)/Co(8)/Cu(7)/NiFe(4.5)/Cu(3)/Pd(3) (all thicknesses given in nm) where t<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Cu</sub> = 10, 30, 50, 70 nm with nano-contact diameters ranging from 60 to 500 nm.

articleTitle: Design and analysis of a dual-stator permanent magnet machine for the refrigerator linear compressor
abstract: In the application of household refrigerator, the linear compressor is popularly adopted due to its no crank mechanism and directly oscillated by the inside drive machine and the helical coil springs. Therefore, a series of linear permanent magnet (PM) machines are developed for the linear compressor drive, which can effectively eliminate the additional cost and losses caused by crank mechanism and gearbox compared to the rotational machines. One production of them is the high-grade LG linear compressor with a linear PM machine inside, which can be 20~30% more efficient than most efficient current crank driven compressors. Dual-stator design is one effective way to improve machine output performance with limited design dimensions. Therefore, based on the topology and dimension of the linear permanent magnet machine in LG linear compressor, an optimized dual-stator permanent magnet machine with two groups of stator tubular windings is proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: Iron loss analysis and reduction techniques of magnetic geared permanent magnet motors
abstract: This paper presents the iron loss analysis of magnetic geared permanent magnet motors (MGPM), and suggests iron loss reduction techniques. In this paper, the hysteresis loss coefficient, the eddy current loss coefficient, and the excess loss coefficient for the modified Steinmetz equation are derived from the Epstein test data using a curve fitting method (CFM). Owing to a much greater iron loss occurring in the rotating field than in the alternating field [3], we separate the rotating and alternating fields and they can be distinguished using the axial ratio of loci. Finally, the iron loss at each electrical steel is calculated using a modified Steinmetz equation that considers the rotating field and flux path. Figure1. (a) shows the schematic of the MGPM, Fig.1. (b) shows the distribution of the flux density on the electrical steel, and Fig.1. (c) shows the analysis points for iron loss at each electrical steel section. We analyzed the magnetic flux density at each point in the rotor core, modulation layer, and stator core. We then, calculated the iron loss using the modified Steinmetz'sequation considering the rotating field and the alternating field. Figure 2. (a) shows a comparison of loci and axial ratio at each region, Fig.2. (b) shows fast Fourier transform (FFT) analysis results at each region, and Fig.2. (c) shows the iron loss analysis results for the original model and the proposed model. The total iron loss of the proposed model is about 15% less than that of the origin model. Furthermore, in this paper, a technique is proposed for reducing the iron loss in the modulation layer, which contributes the most to the total iron loss. More detailed discussions and analysis results will be presented in the final paper.

articleTitle: An electrical model of spin field effect transistors for circuits design and performance analysis
abstract: In this work, we studied the characteristic of spin-FET by presenting an electrical model based on both theoretical and experimental results. We divide the working process of spin-FET into two parts: the first part is the spin injection and detection without the gate voltage. Since the Rashba effect is an intrinsic mechanism, the change of spin direction of the injected spin-polarized current still happens even if there is no extra electric field. The paper gives the calculation of the spin detection result taking into account the Rashba effect, spin injection, and spin accumulation. The second part is the gate voltage modulation. The electron spin precession angle is modulated by the spin-orbit interaction.

articleTitle: An approach to characterize charged magnet rings for permanent magnet motors
abstract: This paper is to introduce an approach to predict the remanence Br and its distribution of a charged permanent magnet (PM) ring for PM motors utilizing the measured surface magnetic flux density with a Hall sensor.

articleTitle: Monte Carlo method for uncertainty propagation in magnetic resonance-based electric properties tomography
abstract: An increasing interest in quantitative tomography, able to evaluate the electric properties distribution inside the human body, arose in the last years.

articleTitle: Higher density melt spun RE-Fe-B isotropic magnets
abstract: Traditional techniques for consolidating melt spun RE-Fe-B powders tend to incur significant volumes of non-magnetic material, like porosity and the polymer binder. Several alternative consolidation techniques are being studied in an effort to reduce this non-magnetic component and improve the performance of these magnets. Rapid Electric Discharge Sintering (REDS) is one such technique that offers a novel way to fully densify melt spun RE-Fe-B with fast cycle times and minimal material wastage. This study highlights the initial development stages of REDS formed magnets and outlines the technical and economic challenges facing such novel technologies.

articleTitle: A low phase noise magnetoacoustic oscillator
abstract: One of the most important goals in the development of communication and radar systems is the reduction of a phase noise level in reference oscillators. In digital communication systems, phase noise affects the data transmission speed and the system bit-error rate. In radar applications, the oscillator's phase noise increases the minimum level of a signal that must be returned by a target in order to be detected. The phase noise of an oscillator is mainly determined by the quality factor of an unloaded resonator. In this work, we propose an oscillator based on a high-Q magneto-acoustic resonator (MAR), which was manufactured from layered yttrium-iron garnet (YIG) - gadolinium gallium garnet (GGG) structure. YIG film with saturation magnetization of M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> = 1740/(4π) G and a thickness of d = 13 um was epitaxially grown on a GGG substrate with a thickness of D = 358 um. The optical polishing technique was used to create highly parallel plates of the YIG-GGG structure. The square thin film YIG resonator with dimensions of 1*1 mm was etched by a laser. The YIG resonator works as a transducer which generates transverse (shear) elastic waves in the YIG-GGG structure.

articleTitle: Characteristic analysis and experimental verification of generating performance in double-sided permanent magnet synchronous linear generator considering three-dimensional effects for ocean wave energy converter
abstract: For generating performance analysis and experimental verification of a double-sided permanent magnet linear synchronous generator (PMLSG) with a slotless stator as shown in Fig. 1(a), this paper utilized a three-dimensional (3D) analysis method and manufactured model. The PMLSG with a slotless stator should be analyzed keeping in consideration end effects such as fringing and leakage flux, particularly because it has a moderately large magnetic air-gap. Because of these effects, the PMLSM requires a 3D analysis method, and a variety of other approaches, including numerical and analytical methods, which have been used in previous studies, for electromagnetic field analysis.

articleTitle: High performance single element MI magnetometer with peak-to-peak voltage detector by synchronized switching
abstract: The MI sensor is a highly sensitive micro magnetic sensor based on the magneto-impedance effect in amorphous wires. In the MI effect, with an excitation by a high-frequency current, the impedance of the amorphous wire sensitively changed with an external magnetic field. A CMOS MI sensor using the analog switch and CMOS IC multi-vibrator was developed in 1999. Then, an electronic compass circuit using 3-axis amorphous wire CMOS MI sensor has been developed for the mobile phone since 2005 by Aichi Steel Corporation, the smart phone since 2011, and the wrist watch since 2013. In this study, we have newly developed a high performance single element MI magnetometer with peak-to-peak voltage detector by synchronized switching (shortened: Pk-pk VD-type MI magnetometer), which is aimed to measure a microscopic magnetic field ranging from nT (109T) to pT (1012T), based upon the conventional MI magnetometer which is used in the electronic compass.

articleTitle: Single-source multiple-coil homogeneous induction heating
abstract: Due to cleanliness, safety and high efficiency, induction heating has been developed rapidly for industrial and domestic heating applications. In this paper, a homogeneous induction heating system has been proposed and implemented. The key is to adopt the magnetic resonant coupling (MRC) mechanism to achieve uniform power distribution of the pan using a single inverter. Specifically, the resonant coil is artfully utilized as the auxiliary coil so that both the primary and auxiliary coils can transmit proper powers to the inner and outer parts of the pan, hence achieving the desired homogeneous heating effect. Theoretical analysis, numerical simulation and experimentation are given to validate the proposed system.

articleTitle: Microstructural influence on surface and bulk magnetisation behaviour in hexagonal ferrites observed by in-situ Magnetic Force Microscopy (MFM) and SQUID magnetometry
abstract: Despite being one of the oldest and well-researched magnetic materials hexagonal ferrites are still of high interest for a number of applications and consequently for academic research.

articleTitle: Mathematical model for the MgB2 hysteresis using parameterized Preisach model
abstract: this paper presents a hysteresis model for the mgb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> using a parameterized Preisach model, in which the weighting functions is determined only based on the M-H limiting loop. The results of simulation and experiment of accuracy of the parameterized Preisach model are reported for the case of iron-sheathed MgB2 superconducting cable samples with an external magnetic field perpendicular to its surface.

articleTitle: A design of rotor bar inclination in squirrel cage induction motor
abstract: This paper analyzes the effect of rotor bar inclination on starting torque, operating torque and operating efficiency in squirrel cage induction motor(SCIM) with finite element analysis method. The results show that the optimum inclination of rotor bar improve all the performances together. An application to the 3.4kW SCIM shows that the starting torque is increased from 17.53Nm to 17.64Nm, and the operating torque is increased from 11.19Nm to 11.26Nm. Also, the operating efficiency is increased from 94.18% to 94.81%.

articleTitle: An innovative off-grid permanent magnet flux switching generator for micro gas turbine in rural areas
abstract: This digest reviews extensively on preliminary analysis to obtain a 30 kW electric power generator and to apply Bio-methane to use it directly to micro gas turbine for electricity generation.

articleTitle: Highly (001)-textured Mn-Ga polycrystalline ultrathin films with a perpendicular magnetic anisotropy
abstract: Perpendicularly magnetized ultrathin films of magnetic metals are technologically important for various spintronic applications, such as the free layer in magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs) for the spin-transfer-torque (STT) magnetoresisive random access memory (MRAM) and in current-perpendicular magnetoresisive devices for the spin-torque radio frequency (rf) oscillators and detectors.

articleTitle: Reduction of switching loss of DC to AC power inverter with PID-like fuzzy controller
abstract: This paper presents a way to reduce energy consumption which is a modified zero-voltage switching pulse width-modulation inverter with a digital signal- processor-based proportional-integral-derivative (PID)-like fuzzy controller (PIDFC). DC to AC energy transformation with a highly inverter device having a Fuzzy controller design, it can be shown that a soft-switching feature can be used to reduce switching losses and improve the converting efficiency significantly. Facing the reduction of energy loss for inverter controller design, comparisons between simulation and experimental results which included traditional PID controller approaching to improve around 75% with simulation results, actually, experimental results still can be improved around 35%, are validated.

articleTitle: 4Gb perpendicular STT-MRAM with compact cell structure and beyond
abstract: Since the discovery of a theoretical idea of spin-transfer torque (STT) [1], STT-MRAM has attracted a great interest as a candidate of universal memory.

articleTitle: The magnetic field sensor based on the longitudinal magnetophotonic effect in a magnetoplasmonic crystal
abstract: Summary form only given. In the present work the LMPIE is used for design of the magnetic field sensor. The in-plane rotating magnetic field is applied as strong as to keep the sample saturated and the intensity of the transmitted light is measured. Due to the LMPIE the second harmonic in signal occurs. The presence of a small additional in-plane constant external magnetic field leads to distortion of the signal. The other harmonics appear, in particular the 1-st and the 3-rd, with their amplitudes being proportional to the constant field. Thus by observing the quantitative changing of the harmonics amplitudes and phases we determine the values of two planar components of the constant magnetic field. In order to prove this concept, we designed and fabricated the samples with rather low saturation magnetization of the dielectric. The samples had different parameters of the gold grating: the period differs from 320 nm to 340 nm and the air slit width differs from 70 nm to 140 nm. The rotating magnetic field of 10 Oe was formed by Helmholtz coils. The light was normally incident on the sample. The spectrum of the LMPIE for one of the samples. The obtained light modulation is 5%. Our next step was adding the constant in-plane magnetic field.

articleTitle: Topological phase transitions in iron garnets crystals with a magnetic compensation temperature
abstract: Summary form only given. Aside from skyrmions and magnetic vortices, magnetic inhomogeneities also include topological defects of domain structure (DS) -magnetic dislocations and disclinations. In this paper, transitions of magnetic domain structures in thin single crystal layers of iron garnets with a magnetic compensation point are studied experimentally. A domain structure of a (111)-plate of (EuTbDy)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> iron garnet (thickness L = 50 μm, quality factor Q = 0.8) was revealed by means of magneto-optical Faraday effect. Temperature topological phase transitions (direct and inverse) are revealed in a single crystal iron garnet plate on both sides of magnetic compensation temperature. It is shown that topological defects - dislocations and disclinations - define the mechanism of topological phase transitions.

articleTitle: Probing core and shell contributions to exchange bias in Co/Co3O4 nanoparticles of controlled size
abstract: Coupling at the interface of core/shell magnetic nanoparticles is known to be responsible for exchange bias (EB) and the relative sizes of core and shell components are supposed to influence the associated phenomenology.

articleTitle: Interplay of ferromagnetism and superconductivity in Ni nanowires with Nb leads
abstract: In this work we explore the interplay of ferromagnetism and superconductivity of single-crystalline Ni nanowires measured with superconducting Nb leads.

articleTitle: Temperature effects on the magnetoimpedance in glass-coated amorphous wires
abstract: Summary form only given. The magnetoimpedance (MI) effect is known as a large and sensitive change in a complex resistance of a magnetic conductor carrying a high frequency current. The temperature dependence of magnetoimpedance (MI) in glass-coated amorphous microwires of two compositions Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">66.94</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3.83</sub>Ni<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.44</sub>B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11.51</sub>Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14.59</sub>Mo<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.69</sub> and Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">23.67</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7.14</sub>Ni<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">43.08</sub>B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13.85</sub>Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12.26</sub> having high (613 K) and low (335 K) Curie temperatures, respectively, was investigated. The wires of the first type have a small negative magnetostriction and are widely used as MI sensing elements. For sensor operation, the temperature stability is of primary importance, however, it was found that the MI change at moderate temperatures of 20-90 degC and low magnetic fields can be nearly 200%. This is explained by high temperature sensitivity of the residual stress and stress-dependent magnetostriction, which resulted in abrupt change in the easy anisotropy direction. The wires of the second type with low Curie temperature Tc and positive magnetostriction demonstrate large and sensitive change in impedance only in the vicinity of Tc due to a corresponding drop in the magnetization saturation and magnetostriction, whilst the bistable type of the magnetization reversal remains. The frequency dispersion of the dynamical permeability shifts towards lower frequencies when approaching Tc suppressing the high frequency properties and MI. Such temperature dependence of MI is well controllable and is proposed for applications in temperature sensors.

articleTitle: Magnetic properties and MR effect of CoxFe3−xO4 nanoparticles
abstract: Magnetic nanoparticles have attracted attention for biomedical applications.

articleTitle: Controlling FePt grain size with a granular MgO-C interlayer in L10 FePt-C media
abstract: Currently, granular L1<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> FePt thin film media is the candidate for heat assisted magnetic recording (HAMR).

articleTitle: Voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy in Tb-Fe-Co/MgO/Gd-Fe MTJ devices
abstract: Voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy (VCMA) effect was successfully observed in ferromagnetic metals such as thin Fe-Pt and Fe-Pd films for the first time.detail. In this article, we study Tb-Fe-Co/MgO/Gd-Fe MTJs with a thick MgO insulating layer avoiding Joule heating and show the VCMA for the relatively thick Gd-Fe free layer became more significant with very thin insertion layers of Co-Fe/Gd under the Gd-Fe free layer. This finding may be very useful for opening up a new application such as the spatial light modulator.

articleTitle: Simulation and performance analysis of a decoupled rotary-linear switched reluctance actuator
abstract: Rotary-linear switched reluctance motors (RLSRMs) are usually implemented in industry applications, such as boring mill, drill press and carving machines, etc [1].

articleTitle: Substrate integrated waveguide based on ferromagnetic nanowires
abstract: In this work, we demonstrate the ability to design a wide range of compact and versatile microwave devices (filters, couplers, antennas, phase shifters, isolators, ...) in substrate integrated waveguide topology by taking advantage of precise manufacturing processes based on laser patterning for the controlled growth of nanowire arrays into nanoporous alumina template.

articleTitle: Bismuth iron garnet Bi3Fe5O12: A room temperature magnetoelectric material
abstract: The possibility to control the magnetic properties of a material with an electric field (or conversely, electric properties with magnetic field) at room temperature is highly desirable for modern applications.

articleTitle: Manufacturing of die-upset rare earth — Iron — Boron magnets with (Ce,La)-mischmetal
abstract: Summary form only given. This work compares several approaches to manufacturing of die-upset R-Fe-B magnets in which more than 40% R is represented by a 65:35 mixture of Ce and La. Pure components as well as two master alloys - Nd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">75</sub>Pr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">25</sub> and Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">44</sub>B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">54</sub>Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> - were used as the raw materials. Nanocrystalline precursors were prepared by compacting melt-spun alloys at 650 °C. The subsequent deformation at 775 - 850 °C with a 65 - 75% height reduction induced in the R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sub>B crystallites a [001] texture along the press direction.The obtained coercivity values indicates that no appreciable H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> could be developed when all the rare earths are represented by the (Ce,La)-mischmetal. Moreover, the relatively high Hc measured for hot-pressed precursor of the hyper-stoichiometric (Ce,La)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">19-x</sub>(Nd,Pr)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">68</sub>Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.4</sub>Cu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> alloys drops dramatically after the die-upsetting. A 30 min annealing at 650 - 700 °C can partially restore the Hc of these “single-alloy” magnets, to 6.3 kOe for 8.6 at.% (Nd,Pr). The second approach was intended to generate hyper-stoichiometric compositions containing 17 - 19 at.% R by blending near-stoichiometric (Ce,La)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9.6-11.2</sub>(Nd,Pr)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.4-2.8</sub>(Fe,Co,Si)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">bal</sub>B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> alloys with a (Nd,Pr)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</sub>Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub>Ni<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub>Cu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</sub> low-melting-temperature alloy.

articleTitle: Equalization method of the wireless power transfer in an electronic shelf label power supply system
abstract: Recently, the research of the wireless power transfer (WPT) technology is brought broad interests because of its convenience at connectivity and operation safety. In this paper, we proposed a new approach to equalize the magnetic flux rather than to physically adjust gaps. But compared to our previous scheme, we added a switch to the receiving coil 1 and coil 3 respectively. This switch is used to control if make the receiving coil short or connect it to the load resistant. When the receiving coil 1 and coil 3 is electronically short, the short current will be generated. It will induce a reversed magnetic flux and therefore cancel with the magnetic flux originally induced by the transmitting yoke.

articleTitle: Design and optimization of direct drive 8/6 External-Rotor Switched Reluctance Motor (Ex-R SRM) for low speed application
abstract: This paper presents a design and optimization of an 8/6 External-Rotor Switched Reluctance Motor for a low speed domestic application as direct drive. The initial design dimensions are derived from the analytical calculation using magnetic equivalent circuit. This is further analyzed and verified with finite element analysis. A prototype has been developed and tested for Inductance profile to baseline the simulation model accuracy. It is also tested for various on/off conduction angles for an R-dump converter to study the impact on torque ripple. Further, a detailed fractional factorial study has been conducted through Design of Experiments (DOE) to identify the critical dimension which are sensitive to Peak and Average torque. This data is further analyzed through regression analysis and fit a transfer function. This transfer function is helpful in finding optimum design without spending further much time in finite element analysis. Finally, the optimum design is further optimized on conduction angles based on the initial study and arrived at the optimum on/off angles for conduction which gives high average torque and compared with initial design.

articleTitle: Simulation of stress effect on GMI in soft magnetic amorphous film
abstract: Soft magnetic amorphous film not only has the giant magneto-impedance (GMI) effect, but also significantly affected by stress-induced magnetic anisotropy[1].

articleTitle: Influence of thermal gradients on the vortex dynamics in CoFeB MTJs
abstract: It was recently shown that the presence of thermal gradients in magnetic nano-devices influences the magnetization state and dynamics in several ways, as for example by the generation of spin currents, spin waves, spin transfer torque, etc. Here we focus on the influence of thermal gradients on the magnetization dynamics of a vortex structure.Here we try to observe experimentally the influence of thermal gradients on a gyrating vortex present in a magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ) pillar and interpret the results by performing numeric simulations. To this aim MTJ samples with a Permalloy layer on top of the free CoFeB layer were prepared at INL and patterned into pillars in order to ensure the formation of a magnetic vortex structure.

articleTitle: SOT induced magnetization reversal in Pt/[Co/Ni]2/Co/Ta multilayer Hall bars without external magnetic field
abstract: Summary form only given. In this work, we show that by selecting PMA material with a weak out-of-plane anisotropy, SOT-induced magnetization reversal can be achieved without the assistance of external magnetic field. Our material stacks comprise of Pt/[Co/Ni]n/Co/Ta, where n = 2, 3 and 4. The magnetization switching is observed by the Hall resistance change with an in-plane DC current flow in the structure with n = 2. The measured R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">H</sub> as a function of the DC current. A clear hysteresis loop was obtained, implying a deterministic switching of the magnetization induced by the applied current. Firstly the magnetization is aligned along the +z orientation. No change in R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">H</sub> is observed when positive current (along +x direction) flows through the wire. As the current is swept in the opposite direction, negative current (along -x direction), RH exhibits a step wise decrease at a current of -4 mA, reaching saturation at -6.5 mA. This implies that the magnetization has switched to the -z orientation. As the current is then increased towards +6.5 mA, the initial change in RH signal occurs at 2 mA, with a quasi-stable state at +3 mA and saturation at +4 mA. This results in an asymmetric hysteresis loop.

articleTitle: MAMR frequency optimization on [CoX/Pt]4 media
abstract: Microwave assisted magnetic recording (MAMR) technology, with microwave generated by the spin transfer oscillator (STO) as energy assisted source, is potential for future magnetic recording technique. In this work, we use [CoX/Pt]<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> media as simulation model, in which the relatively strong field interaction between layers competes with the different effective field distribution of each layer. abstract: Summary form only given. In this work we investigate a wireless strain sensor where a polycrystalline FeAlB alloy has been used for the transducer. The materials used for the sensor were commercially available Metglas 2826MB3 (resonator) which had received a transverse field anneal as described previously1 and a FeAlB alloy for the transducer.

articleTitle: Micromagnetic studies of time-dependent coercivity
abstract: Summary form only given. This work has studied the time-dependent coercivity in both the constant-field model and changing-field model, based on a new micromagnetic method at finite temperature using hybrid Monte Carlo (HMC) algorithm. By comparing the simulated time-dependent coercivity with the Sharrock's law, the scaling relationship between the fictitious simulation time in the Hamilton equations in the HMC micromagnetics and the real time t is derived, and the simulation time in a trajectory is found to be close to 1 ns in the real time scale. Furthermore, we have studied the effects of the magnetic anisotropy types on the parameter τ in Sharrock's law, and it is found that the cubic anisotropy model exhibits a larger τ than uniaxial anisotropy model. Our simulation results agree well with the experiments and the results from other simulation methods under certain circumstances.

articleTitle: Linear and nonlinear spin-wave mode localization in a spin-torque oscillator with a field well
abstract: We have shown that the appearance of a magnetic field well in a free layer of an STO can significantly affect the current-induced magnetization dynamics in this layer, and can lead to the change of a character of the excited spin wave mode. Instead of a nonlinear self-localized bullet spin wave mode a linearly localized spin wave mode can be excited. Our results are particularly important for the spin-Hall oscillators, that, due to the in-plane static magnetization, naturally have a negative nonlinear frequency shift, and, in the case when the spin-Hall angle is negative, also have a magnetic field well created by the Oersted field of the bias current that is comparable in size with the active region where the bias current is applied.

articleTitle: A long baseline fluxgate gradiometer with electrical alignment and its calibration method
abstract: Summary form only given. In this paper, the developed fluxgate gradiometer probe and its calibration method are presented. Method Both the sensing and reference elements were composed of three toroidal core fluxgate magnetometers, which were orthogonally oriented to each other, and implemented in an aluminum straight pipe with a diameter and length of 40 mm and 1.24 m, respectively. The sensing element was at the head of the pipe, and the reference element was 1 m away from the sensing element. The excitation coils for six individual toroidal cores, made of permalloy, were connected in series. The core was excited by a DC-biased sinusoidal current at a frequency of 100 kHz, and the demodulation of the induced secondary voltage from the sensing coil was operated in the fundamental mode [2][3]. The demodulated signal from the fluxgate driving circuit was connected to flux locked loops (FLL), which are commonly used for superconducting quantum interference devices, to expand their dynamic range and achieve linearity [4]. The double-integrator type FLL was applied, and the frequency band of the FLL was adjusted to 0.1 Hz-10 Hz for the sensing element and to DC-10 Hz for the reference element. The probe and the electronics were connected by a 50-m-long waterproof multi-core cable. For calibration, an array of coils was prepared to emit a fundamental magnetic field. Three coils, each 30 mm in diameter, were orthogonally combined into one bobbin.

articleTitle: Application of high permeability magnetic core sensor for IoTs device
abstract: The measurement of electric current is not always stable, especially when the measured signal requires further electronic conditioning such as printed circuit board (PCB). The current signal must be satisfied to detect the signal into a micro-computer in which sensors transfer current signal into a proportional voltage. The basic sensor requirement includes galvanic isolation and operated a high bandwidth; it is usually define the bandwidth from DC up to at least 100 kHz. Recently, the Internet of things (IoT) is one of the attention trends in the industry. It deploys solutions that harness multiple technologies from smart sensors, for example, magnetic sensor, and digital data processing to communications, all with the goal of enhancing everyday life. Current transformer sensor is most of popular device for current detection. This paper presents a magnetic current sensor with amorphous material to use to detect the power system in high current signal detection which are also has appliance implemented in Internet of Things.

The emission of spin waves was produced by the reversal or oscillation of nanoscale magnetic vortex cores in a NiFe disk array. The vortex cores in the disk array were excited by an out of plane radio frequency (rf) magnetic field. The dynamic behaviors of the magnetization of NiFe were studied using a micro-focused Brillouin light scattering spectroscopy (BLS) setup.

articleTitle: Magnetoimpedance in samples with patterned surfaces for the detection of ferrofluids
abstract: Summary form only given. The magneto-impedance (MI) represents the large change in the electrical impedance experienced by soft magnetic conductors when they are subjected to an external magnetic field. Amorphous ribbons and wires are the best suited materials for MI, displaying impedance variations as large as 800% with very large sensitivities at low magnetic fields. Consequently, they have been proposed as high performance materials for magnetic sensors. Among other applications, the MI has been often investigated as a sensible effect for the detection of magnetic particles aimed to biomedical applications. For instance, it has been recently proven its suitability to detect the concentration of magnetic nanoparticles in ferrogels, as a model system for natural tissue. The sensitivity in these cases is considered to arise from the permeability of the magnetic particles which modifies the electromagnetic conditions for the current flow in the MI sample. For this kind of applications, the surface roughness seems to have an important role. It has been reported that etching the ribbon surface in acid produces pits and holes that increase the MI sensitivity to magnetic particles. In this work we investigate the possibility of maximize this effect by a controlled patterning of the sample surface. The basic idea is that the surface patterning increases the overall impedance of the sample, because it hampers the current flow that mostly takes place close to the surface due to the skin effect. In the presence of a ferrofluid, the patterned surface is partially smoothened (in terms of magnetic permeability) for the electromagnetic field, reducing the electrical impedance. The change in the impedance of the sample due to the presence of the ferrofluid must therefore be greater in the patterned sample over the change experienced by a sample with the original, unpatterned, surface. First, finite element simulations (FEM) have been performed to determine the expected sensibility of patterned samples. We have considered a 10 μm thick homogeneous sample whose surface is patterned with longitudinal trenches, with a typical section of of 1×1 μm. We have tested the effect of a ferrofluid with a relative permeability of μm = 100 over the sample for both cases: plain sample and sample with the patternend surface. The impedance of the sample is obtained as a function of the frequency for two extreme values of the sample permeability (μ = 5000 and μ = 1). After optimizing the distance between trenches, the results confirms our assumption as shown in figure 1: the relative change in impedance when the ferrofluid is present is larger in the sample with the patterned surface. Secondly, the controlled patterning of the ribbon surface by photolithography is investigated. A mask of circular dots with 10 μm diameter is used to expose a photosensitive resist spun on the surface of an amorphous ribbon. After developing, the sample covered by the patterned resist is etched for 1 hour in diluted nitric acid. The results confirm that circular holes about 1 μm deep have been successfully etched in the ribbon.
