articleTitle: Route toward high-speed nano-magnonics
abstract: Downscaling poses a number of new challenges for the implementation of magnonic devices. In particular, the traditional inductive method for spin wave excitation becomes inefficient at nanoscale due to the increasing requirements for the power density, the unavoidable limitations imposed on the wavelength of the excited waves by the geometry of the inductive antennae, and the difficulty of the impedance matching of the latter. An alternative approach to the excitation of spin waves can be based on the spin-transfer torque (STT) mechanism, which provides the ability to directly convert dc electrical currents into microwave-frequency spin waves on nanoscale.

articleTitle: All-optical magnetization switching of FePt magnetic recording medium
abstract: Magnetization manipulation is an indispensable tool for both basic and applied research. The dynamics of the response depends on the energy transfer from the laser excited electrons to the spins within the first femtoseconds. This determines the speed of the ultrafast magnetization. A special material of interest for magnetic storage development is FePt. In a seminal experiment all optical writing had been demonstrated for FePt nanoparticle of a magnetic hard disc media, completely surprisingly, by Lambert et al. in Science 2014. But, the mechanism remained unclear and it opened many questions about the extension of possibilities of all optical writing as a general mechanism. Meanwhile writing experiments by single laser spots point to an asymmetric writing per each shot. This is consistently observed by different groups [4,5,6]. These effects can be described within different rate models. I will review the current understanding of the interaction of ultrafast excitation and heating, influence of magnetic dichroism and the presence of the inverse Faraday effect and attempts of understanding of these processes so far. From the experimental side in especial single shot writing experiments, that show a kind of accumulation effects of the writing, allow to pinpoint the underlying mechanism of writing in these media. Together, ab-initio calculations of the optical effects (inverse Faraday effect and magnetic dichroism induced heating) and the thermal modeling, allow to calculate the switching rates of the individual FePt nanoparticles. The latter then provides a rate of switching of the ensemble. A careful experimental determination of the absorbed fluence in the spherical geometry of the nanoparticles gives us a complete picture of the competing effects, of heating and writing asymmetries, and we can trace the different processes from the beginning of the laser pulse impact [4]. In addition, this theoretical description allows us to optimize the number of shots needed to write the magnetization of the FePt nanoparticles and to pinpoint how to optimize the all optical writing. In my talk, I will review these recent developments that may lead to address an individual nanosized magnetic element in the far future all optically, for writing magnetic memory and memory storage.

articleTitle: A soft-5/6 modulation code with iterative ITI subtraction scheme in multi-reader TDMR systems
abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) modulation encoding is one of the effective solutions that was used to take action with severe intertrack interference (ITI) effect in two-dimensional magnetic recording (TDMR) system. As found in our previous work, the rate-4/5 modulation code with the ITI subtraction scheme was proposed to avoid severe ITI data patterns for TDMR, its performance outperforms an uncoded system. To obtain the higher code rate and get a better performance; however, we propose the soft-5/6 modulation coding scheme performs together with 3 readers in TDMR system. Moreover, we also propose the iterative ITI subtraction scheme by utilizing feedback data from center track, which performs together with the proposed soft-5/6 modulation code. Finally, the system performances of the various reader offsets for the upper and lower readers are investigated.

articleTitle: GMR-based single-domain magnetic sensor for 500nm single particle detection
abstract: Summary form only given. In this study, we develop a GMR-based single-domain magnetic sensor that presents the result digitally by two states: the absence and the presence of the magnetic labels. The proposed sensor not only shares all the desirable properties of standard magnetoresistive sensors, but achieves single magnetic nanoparticle detection as well. Moreover, our single-domain magnetic sensor is readily available for immediate integration with biomolecule applications. A GMR-based magnetic sensor consists of two synthetic antiferromagnetic layers separated by 6nm Cu layer is developed. Co 5nm/Ru 0.8nm/Co 5nm is chosen to be the pinned layer to retain the direction of magnetization during the measurement, and the free layer Co 5nm/Ru 1.4nm/Co 10nm is designed to switch in a relatively low magnetic field that the tester system can easily achieve. The GMR stack (Ta 2.5nm/Ru 5nm/ Co 5nm/Ru 0.8/Co 5nm/Cu 6nm/Co 5nm/Ru 1.4nm/Co 10nm/Ta 5nm) is sputtering deposited on silicon wafer with 500nm SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>. After deposition, the film is patterned into an array of 700 X 600 nm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> rectangles by e-beam lithography system and 70 nm thick Cu is made as leads to pass current to the GMR sensors. The sensors are finally coated with a 100 nm thick pinhole-free alumina to prevent corrosion and serve as a base for attaching biomolecules.

articleTitle: Development and integration of micro-patterned, thick CoPtP permanent magnets for MEMS applications
abstract: CMOS compatible integration of permanent magnets with thickness of the order of microns to hundreds of microns is a key challenge for a number of magnetic MEMS applications such as mechanical energy harvesters. Particularly the performance of magnetic MEMS devices are restricted by the limited volume of the integrated magnets. When a relatively thin film of permanent magnet is used as source of magnetic field, the stray magnetic field appears only from the edge of the magnet and a large part of the material is wasted. Hence, the magnetic flux intensity is greatly reduced which affect the performance of integrated magnetic transducers. It is therefore proposed to replace a film or a block of permanent magnet by micro-patterned array of magnets.

articleTitle: Clustering effect on frequency dependent magnetic properties of FeCo micro hollow fiber composites
abstract: FeCo hollow fibers can possess high anisotropy field due to their high aspect ratio. Thus composite sheets containing these fibers are applicable to nearfield electromagnetic wave absorption sheets in 1~10 GHz region. For an understanding of the high frequency properties of the composite sheets, the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (LLG) equation including eddy current effect and the effective medium theory with an additional magnetostatic correction were applied to simulate the frequency dependency of their magnetic properties.

articleTitle: Properties of signal caused by the Cracks on the back surface of steel plate in low frequency eddy current testing
abstract: Summary form only given. In this study, we investigate low frequency ECT to detect a crack existing on the back surface of a steel plate. Accordingly, an electromagnetic field simulation was performed to quantitatively examine the properties of the signal caused by the crack, such as the dependences of signal strength on the thickness of the crack and the excitation frequency. We also examined the effect of change of permeability or conductivity at the crack on the signal. Figure 1 shows a model of the electromagnetic field simulation using the finite element method. Two excitation coils were arranged on the upper side of the steel plate. The thickness of the steel plate was set as 10 mm. A crack of length 20 mm and width 5 mm was made on the back of the steel plate. The thickness of the crack, d, was 0, 2, 4, 8, or 10 mm. The Z component of the magnetic flux density distribution in the XY plane (Z = 5 mm), B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</sub>(x, y), was calculated for each value of d. Subsequently, the ECT signal from the crack was calculated as ΔB<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</sub> (x, y) = B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</sub> (x, y | with cracks) - B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</sub> (x, y | without cracks). Figure 2 shows the ECT signal ΔB<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</sub> for different values of d when the excitation frequency f was changed from 2 to 16 Hz. The horizontal axis represents the real part, Re[ΔB<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</sub>], whereas the vertical axis represents the imaginary part Im[ΔB<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</sub>]. The letters in the figure represent the frequency (in Hz). When d = 10 mm, i.e., when the crack passes through the steel plate, we obtain a large signal ΔB<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</sub>. In this case, Re[ΔB<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</sub>] is almost independent of f, whereas Im[ΔB<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</sub>] increases with increasing f. When d <; 10 mm, on the other hand, the value of ΔB<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</sub> significantly decreases with the decrease of d. Therefore, the skin effect of the steel above the crack, whose thickness is given by (10 - d) mm, significantly deteriorates the crack signal ΔB<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</sub>. In this case, Re[ΔB<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</sub>] decreases with increasing frequency, whereas Im[ΔB<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</sub>] begins to saturate for higher frequencies. We could quantitatively explain these properties by considering the skin effect of the steel above the crack. Furthermore, both the permeability and conductivity change at the crack and the crack part is usually represented as air (relative permeability is μ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> = 1 and conductivity is a = 0). Therefore, we examine the effect of change of permeability or conductivity at the crack on the signal. In order to study the effect of change of permeability, the crack part was represented as metal (μ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> = 1). The effect of the change of conductivity was studied by representing the crack as an insulating magnetic material (a = 0). It was observed that, in the case of change of permeability, the values of Re[ΔB<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</sub>] and Im[ΔB<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</sub>] are almost the same as those observed in the case of air. Therefore, the change of permeability at the crack dominates the ECT signal.

articleTitle: Strain engineering in MgO magnetic tunnel junctions
abstract: Summary form only given. The material and interface engineering of magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJ) is the key for the future of spin transfer torque based random access memories (STT-RAM). Especially the ferromagnet/MgO interface plays a very critical role in the device performance and the presence of strain in the structure can change the properties of the device significantly. We first study the effect of strain on MTJ induced by a diamond like carbon (DLC) film, which induces a strong compressive strain [1]. The junction resistance as well as the tunnel magnetoresistance (TMR) reduces with the DLC film. Then we demonstrate that quantum transport across magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs) can be significantly affected by the introduction of tensile strain, achieving an enhancement factor of ~2 in the experimental TMR ratio [2]. It is found that the TMR values increase with increasing levels of strain before reaching a saturated value. The effect is found to be reversible and repeatable, suggesting that the mechanical deformation is elastic for the stress levels applied during the testing. We further correlate this strain-enhanced TMR with coherent spin tunneling through the MgO barrier. Finally, flexible MgO barrier magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ) devices are fabricated using a transfer printing process, which exhibit reliable and stable operation under substantial deformation of the device substrates [3]. CoFeB/MgO/CoFeB MTJs are fabricated on conventional, thermally-oxidized silicon substrates, and then the underlying silicon is etched to release the MTJs from the substrates. The MTJs are then transferred and adhered onto flexible polyethylene terephthalate (PET) substrates as shown in Fig. 1(a). The flexible MTJ devices yield significantly enhanced tunneling magnetoresistance (TMR) of ~300 % and improved abruptness of switching in Fig. 1(b), as residual strain in the MTJ structure induced by the fabrication process is released during the transfer process. The strain-enhanced TMR is analyzed using non-equilibrium Green's function (NEGF) quantum transport calculations. Our results could provide useful insights for the design and engineering of novel MgO barrier MTJ-based straintronics as well as flexible electronics applications.

articleTitle: Calibration system for magnetometer in low magnetic field range
abstract: Summary form only given. In free space, unshielded large volume of a low permanent magnetic field (MF) generating system is necessary for use in such areas of magnetic measurements as: calibration of magnetometers, testing of materials, the ecological and medical effects, etc. This equipment allows not only to compensate automatically Earth magnetic field (EMF) but also to generate precise and stable MF in the range of (0 ~ 1.2) mT. A permanent EMF in the working spaces in the wooden house is compensated by an opposite MF, currents passing through a large 3-axis Helmholtz coil. Also time variations of the EMF are monitored at the observatory by a Cs magnetometer which is located in the center of another small 3-axis Helmholtz coil having an identical coil constant with that of large one in each direction. In addition to the main windings for permanent EMF, each pair has an extra one of feedback coil for the compensation of the time-varying EMF.

articleTitle: Spin transport properties in thermally-evaporated pentacene films by using the spin-pump
abstract: Carbon-based molecules are promising materials from the viewpoint of the spin transport because their spin-orbit interaction is generally weak.

articleTitle: Crystal, electronic structures and spin signals Co2FeAl0.5Si0.5/n-GaAs junctions
abstract: The authors studied the atomic and electronic structures of CFAS-GaAs junctions using RHEED and TEM. The current-voltage measurements were performed by DC four probe method. Spin transport measurement was performed by applying reverse bias current of 0.3 mA at 10 K. The EDX analysis was carried out in CFAS near the CFAS/GaAs. Conductance ratio measured at 0.5 and -0.5 V is used to evaluate the rectifying characteristics of Schottky barrier.

articleTitle: Numerical study on a novel Curie temperature controlled hybrid thermo-magnetic structure for magnetic random access memories
abstract: In this work, with the intention of finding out the capability of the TcC structure for lower switching current (ISTT), we have run time-domain simulations of current induced switching dynamics for a hybrid free layer and single layer by solving the Landau-Lifshitz-Bloch (LLB) equation modified to include spin-torque terms. We will describe how the TcC hybrid structure can reduce the critical switching current (Ic), as compared with a single layer structure with room temperature (CT), a single layer structure with Joule heating (TA) and a magnetically hard-soft composite structure with Joule heating (EcC).

articleTitle: Design principles of a magnetic-passive and sliding conjugated bearing
abstract: To reduce the constructive complexity of purely active bearings, Silva [1] proposed a hybrid magnetic bearing configuration using two suspension strategies: passive radial bearings using permanent magnets, and active control only in the axial direction.

articleTitle: Modeling analysis and estimation of thyroid gland tissue temperature distribution for electromagnetic induction ablation using thermotherapy needle
abstract: This paper proposes a by incorporating estimated models of simulate thyroid tissue and thyroid electromagnetic inducted ablation needle, the medical personnel can obtain the operating parameters of an electromagnetic heating machine, such as the applied current, ablation time, inserting depth, if necessary.

articleTitle: Colossal positive magneto-resistance in oxygen deficient Ca4Mn3O10
abstract: Huge change of resistance by an external magnetic field, i.e. colossal magneto-resistance effect, has been a long-lived theme of research due to both fundamental science and device applications. Here we report colossal positive magneto-resistance (> 1200% at a temperature of 4K and a magnetic field of 9 T) discovered in oxygen deficient Ca<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>Mn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub> phase. The structural, magnetic and magneto transport properties are discussed.

articleTitle: Interpolation of noisy measurements in a coarse grid: Creating waveforms for intermediate points on ‘747’ curves
abstract: In some situations only a limited number of measurements under a limited number of conditions may be available for analysis. This paper describes an approach for creating additional interpolated measurements in which measurement-noise as well as signal both have appropriate values. A simple example of how not to do this would be to average two waveforms captured from a Hard-Disk-Drive at different readback positions and expect this to behave like a waveform captured at the midpoint between the two positions. A waveform created in this manner would yield a reasonable interpolation of the signals from the disk (including media noise), but the noise from the read-head and preamplifier would not be representative since it gets reduced 3 dB by the averaging. Using such a waveform to evaluate sector-failure rate in an experimental software readback channel would give a hugely optimistic result! This paper formulates a better solution for the general problem and then applies this approach specifically to the situation where a series of spin-stand waveforms were captured at various reader positions and with various written track squeeze positions (i.e. a set of `747s').

articleTitle: An artificial neural network with an analogue spin-orbit torque device
abstract: Since collective spin systems store digital information as their magnetization direction, development of nonvolatile memories for computers with the von Neumann architecture is one of the mainstream outlets of spintronics research pursued in the last several decades.

articleTitle: Two-dimensional signal processing schemes for high areal density bit-patterned media magnetic recording based on channel polarization
abstract: To achieve areal density of a few terabits or more per square inch, many two-dimensional magnetic recording (TDMR) systems have proposed for future promising magnetic recording schemes.

articleTitle: Magnetic structures and low frequency dynamics of cubic nanoparticles: Vortex line networks and vortex line dances
abstract: The magnetic structures of 3D nanoparticles are complex and strongly depend on sample size and shape because of the competition between long ranged interactions such as dipolar ones and short ranged interactions such as exchange.

articleTitle: Giant damping-like spin orbit torque in perpendicular magne-tized double Pt/Co stack structure
abstract: Manipulating the magnetization of nanomagnets by local electric current has been widely studied in the past few years because of its promise in non-volatile magnetic memory and logic devices.

articleTitle: Orthogonal fluxgate gradiometer with multiple coil pairs
abstract: Summary form only given. In this paper we present a new type of magnetic gradiometer based on orthogonal fluxgate in fundamental mode. This type of sensor can be build using two different magnetic cores, each one with its own pick-up coil, or using single core with two pick-up coils wound on it. In the first case it is easy to suppress the response to the homogeneous field by matching the sensitivities with different excitation parameters. However, this approach has an obvious disadvantage in terms of noise and offset stability vs. temperature.

articleTitle: A novel compact AC/DC current sensor
abstract: With the development of modern power system and the appearance of high performance power electronic devices, more and more DC grids, renewable energy grids and micro grids are constructed and connected to the main power system.

articleTitle: Optical excitation of magnetization dynamics in magnetic optical microcavity
abstract: Optical generation of the magnetostatic spin waves (MSWs) due to the inverse Faraday effect or photomagnetic phenomena is of prime importance for magnonics and spintronics.

articleTitle: High frequency properties of compacted Fe-4.5 wt% Si powders with insulating layer synthesized by modified dew point treatment
abstract: Currently, MnZn ferrite and NiZn ferrite have been widely used as magnetic shielding materials for WPC operating in the frequency range of 100~205 kHz.

articleTitle: Magnetic imaging system in smartphones based on built-in magnetometer
abstract: Summary form only given. Magnetometers have recently become a built-in feature in most tablets and smartphones around the globe. The sensor is usually based on GMR/AMR (Giant/ Anisotropic Magneto Resistance) materials, which are produced as magnetometer integrated circuits that cost less than USD 1. Although they are not as sensitive as the magnetometers used in the geomagnetic survey, their omnipresence and low price tag, as well as the readily available computing power of tablets/smartphones, drive our interest to develop a subsurface imaging system based on built-in magnetometers.

articleTitle: Iron loss model for electrical machines fed by low switching frequency PWM
abstract: Modern electrical machines are normally driven by a pulse width module (PWM) inverter.The aim of this study is to develop an iron loss model for electrical machines fed by a low switching frequency PWM inverter. In the full paper, iron loss models for sinusoidal flux density are reviewed at first. A lamination test is carried out in this study to evaluate the accuracy of the model for sinusoidal flux density, this will be systematically demonstrated in the full paper.

articleTitle: Theory of magnetic tunneling junctions with semiconductor barriers CuInSe2 and CuGaSe2
abstract: MTJs. In this work, we study transport properties of MTJs including semiconductor barriers CuInSe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> (CIS) and CuGaSe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> (CGS), which are terminal compounds of a mixed crystal CuIn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>Ga<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Se<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>. Since the band gap of CuIn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>Ga<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Se<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> continuously increases with increasing x, CIGS lies between CIS and CGS not only chemically but also physically. Thus, the present work on the CIS and CGS compounds is appropriate to understand the origin of high MR ratios and low RA values observed in the CIGS-based MTJs. We prepared supercells of Fe/CIS/Fe and Fe/CGS/ Fe, each of which includes 17 layers of CIS or CGS and 3 layers of Fe on both sides of the barrier. Termination layers were selected as Se layers on the basis of the TEM observations on the CIGS-based MTJs [3]. We optimized the positions of atoms in the supercells using the density functional theory implemented in the Vienna ab-initio simulation program (VASP).

articleTitle: Stabilization of phase noise in vortex spin torque nano-oscillators by a Phase Locked Loop
abstract: After a decade of research, large expectations have been anticipated on how the rich physics of spin transfer induced magnetization dynamics could give birth to a new generation of multi-functional microwave spintronic devices [1]. This work presents experimental results showing how the phase noise of vortex based STNOs can be efficiently controlled by implementation of an integrated PLL circuit.

articleTitle: Optimization for 4/4 stator/rotor single-phase asymmetric-stator-poles doubly salient permanent magnet machine
abstract: One novel 4/4 stator/rotor single phase doubly salient permanent magnet machine (SP-DSPMM) with asymmetric stator poles is proposed in this paper. The stator poles for the proposed machine are distributed non-uniformly along the circumference of the stator yoke. Firstly, it investigates the new topology and operation principle based on diagram description and mathematical derivation. Then, several improved structures are presented to improve the output torque performance. Finally, comprehensive comparison on main electromagnetic performance indexes for all the proposed structures are performed. It indicates that the torque ripple and minimum torque under rated operation condition can be improved with pole shoe, step air gap and auxiliary teeth introduced in the original structure.

articleTitle: Sub-resolution imaging of low-dimensional magnetic objects by magneto-optical Kerr microscopy
abstract: The imaging and measurement of the size of low dimensional magnetic objects, such as domain walls, magnetic bubbles or skyrmions is both of timeless and current importance, respectively, for fundamental and application-related research.

articleTitle: Spin-torque oscillator sensor for simultaneous readout of two adjacent bit tracks
abstract: Spin-torque oscillators (STOs) have been proposed as candidates for magnetic field sensors with the possible advantages including high spatial resolution, energy efficiency and frequency resolution [1,2,3].

articleTitle: Real-time observation of molecularly thin lubricant films on head sliders using rotating-compensator-based ellipsometric microscopy
abstract: Lubricant pick-up by head sliders has been an important issue for head-disk interface (HDI) designs due to decrease of head-disk clearance. In this paper, we propose an improved method that can provide a higher frame rate of around 1 frame/sec and higher signal-to-noise ratio by introducing rotating-compensator-ellipsometry (RCE) to quantify the lubricant thickness.

articleTitle: Fast optimal design method of variable flux reluctance machines for maximizing the average torque
abstract: Variable flux reluctance machines (VFRMs) have been extensively investigated due to their many advantages: robust structure, compact winding, good flux regulation capability and low torque ripple and acoustic noise [1].

articleTitle: Controlling of voltage-induced spin wave resonance properties in ferromagnetic nanowires with perpendicular anisotropy
abstract: The voltage-induced manipulation of magnetic properties, including the modulation of coercively or the magnetization switching, has been attracting intense research interests [1].

articleTitle: Nonlinear switching of spin waves in the side-coupled magnonic stripes
abstract: The development of magnonic micro and nanosized elements leads to the fabrication of functional devices for planar magnonic applications.

articleTitle: Design and analysis of a linear Halbach magnetic actuator for an aerospace vehicle
abstract: A linear Halbach magnetic actuator (L-HMA) with tubular structure is designed to meet high power density requirements for an aero-space vehicle. Detailed design and analysis of L-HMA carried out and simulation results shows an increment of 16% in torque density compared to conventional topology without Halbach array. The prototype is realized and the experimental results are well matching with simulation results.

articleTitle: New process of the eddy current probe impedance calculation for plate inspection using bidimensional Magnetically Coupled Elements
abstract: The defect detection mechanism for eddy current nondestructive testing (ECNDT) is related to the interaction of induced eddy currents in the metal test specimen with flaws, and the coupling of these interaction effects with the test probe sensor.

articleTitle: Output characteristic model of cantilever-like tactile sensor based on the inverse magnetostrictive effect
abstract: Summary form only given. In this paper, the model of the output voltage for the cantilever-like sensor has been founded and the relationship between the output voltage and the external load has been determined, according to the inverse-magnetostrictive effect, the flexure mode, and the Jiles-Atherton model. The output voltage is relative with the bias magnetic field and the information of the sample, which is dependent on the contact force, the contact area and the friction coefficient, in addition to the Galfenol sheet material parameters. The Galfenol sheet material parameters include the length of Galfenol sheet, the Young's modulus, the Poisson's ratio, the relative permeability, the density of Galfenol sheet, the sectional moment of inertia, and the tilted angle of Galfenol sheet. The output voltage of the cantilever-like sensor is caused by the change of magnetic induction in Galfenol material.

articleTitle: Microstructure evolution and magnetic behavior of self-organized arrays of ultra-high aspect ratio epitaxial Co nanostrips
abstract: The arrays of magnetic nanowires (NWs) and nanostrips (NSs) with uniaxial anisotropy are good candidates to be used in domain wall propagation based devices, magnetic storage media with high recording density, GMR sensors and biomedical assays.

articleTitle: Underlayer-dependent perpendicular magnetic anisotropy of Co2Fe0.4Mn0.6Si Heusler alloy ultra-thin films
abstract: Spin transfer torque magnetoresistive random access memory (STT-MRAM) is being developed as a candidate for the next generation memories nowadays.

articleTitle: Effect of DC bias current on sensitivity of thin-film magnetoimpedance element
abstract: Magnetoimpedance (MI) sensor is commercially applied for compasses in mobile phones [1], and its sensitivity has been enhanced to be applicable to biomedical research field and nondestructive testing [2]. Amorphous wires and ribbons are mostly used in current developed sensor. On the other hand, miniaturization of electronic devices and measurement with higher spatial resolution progress: this increases a strong demand for a miniaturization of MI elements. Because an MI element composed of thin-film is compatible with integrated electronic devices and it can be fabricated by photolithography techniques, thin-film MI element is a solution to such demands. However, a thin-film MI element has generally less sensitivity compared with wires and ribbons, therefore the sensitivity of thin-film elements should be enhanced more. The sensitivity of thin-film MI element strongly depends on the relation between the easy axis direction, the ac small field excitation direction, and the detection field direction. The typical preferable case is that the ac small field is excited parallel to the easy axis direction and the detection field is perpendicular to the easy axis: the easy axis is aligned to the width direction of the element. When the easy axis is inclined to the width direction and the inclined angle is large, MI elements show quite different profiles with a typical sensor, while its profile is similar to typical one when the inclined angle is small. Additionally, a dc bias current applied to the element directly is an effective way to control a MI profile. However, the effects of dc bias current on MI profiles on thin-film elements have less investigated, though the effects on wires and ribbons have some reports [3, 4]. Therefore, we investigated the effects of dc bias current on the MI profile of thin-film elements with inclined easy axis with small angle, and also discussed a potential for enhancement of sensitivity for a field detection with controlling easy axis direction and dc bias current intensity.

articleTitle: Absence of the thermal Hall effect in anomalous Nernst and spin Seebeck effects
abstract: The anomalous Nernst effect (ANE) and the spin Seebeck effect (SSE) in spin caloritronics are two of the most important mechanisms to manipulate the spin-polarized current and pure spin current by thermal excitation.

articleTitle: A novel finger rehabilitation method using an electromag-netic system
abstract: Hand rehabilitation and training systems generally utilize either robot hands or robotic gloves [1–3]. These devices generate the repetitive gripping motion of fingers. The configuration of robot hands, which consist of electrical motors, wires, gears, etc., is complex, making them difficult to wear. To avoid these problems, many researchers have been developing soft robotic gloves that utilize flexible materials with a pneumatic system. However, because this method also utilizes wired control, stroke patients can find the gloves difficult to wear. In this study, we propose a novel method for finger rehabilitation and/or hand training. The proposed system provides a simply configured wireless system in an easily wearable device that uses magnetic torque and force control, which is based on an electromagnetic system that uses a permanent magnet. The proposed system provides two assist modes: active mode, which is between the electromagnetic field and the permanent magnet, and passive mode, which is between the permanent magnets. Figure 1 shows the principles used for the generation of the gripping motion and the configuration of the proposed method. Fig. 1 (a) shows the electromagnetic (EM) mode. The applied alternating magnetic field generates rotation and parallel translation by magnetic torque and force. These actuations are a basic principle of finger gripping. Fig. 1 (b) shows the permanent magnet (PM) mode. To increase the gripping angle of the fingers, we use a permanent magnet on the palm. The two magnets between the driving magnet and the assist magnet on the palm generate an attractive force. Thus, the proposed method is a hybrid that is used to control the gripping movement of the fingers, as shown in Fig. 1 (c). Because of this hybrid, we can decrease power consumption. Figure 1 (d) shows the configuration of the proposed methods. The inner diameter of the driving coil is 10 cm, and the coil has 250 turns by a wire diameter of 1.6 mm. The size of the driving magnet is (width) 20 mm × (length) 10 mm × (thickness) 10 mm. The surface magnetic flux density is 302 mT. The assist magnet is a disc-type, and its diameter and height are 10 and 3 mm, respectively. The surface magnetic flux density is 209 mT. The hybrid method becomes the active control, whereas the passive control does not use the driving coil. Hence, the active control does not require additional gripping force from patients. However, the passive control does utilize a patient's gripping force. Once the hand grips, an attractive force between the driving magnet and the assist magnet is generated. When we open our hands, the fingers require a stretching force more than an attractive force. Therefore, the passive control is suitable for increasing the muscular power of the fingers. Under the active control, variations in magnetic torque cause a stretching motion without the addition of finger force from patients. In the fabricated system, the maximum attractive force was 1.5 N.

articleTitle: Slotted permanent-magnet machines: Fourier-based analytical modeling considering finite permeability of teeth
abstract: Due to their high efficiency, permanent-magnet (PM) machines are increasingly used in many applications.

articleTitle: Spin Hall effect induced SOT fields in perpendicular magnetized Co/Ni multilayer systems
abstract: Recently, Spin-Orbit torque (SOT) arising from the ferromagnetic heterostructures consisting of an ultra-thin ferromagnet (FM) sandwiched between a heavy metal (HM) and an Oxide layer has attracted extensive attention in the low power magnetic memory and logic devices. In this work, we characterized the SOT effective fields in Co/Ni multilayer systems with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (PMA) using harmonic Hall voltage measurement technique. Compared to single thin FM, the multilayers have a higher plasticity in the thickness, which makes it more practical for real applications. Therefore the PMA stacks consisting of Ta/Pt/Ta/[Co/Ni]<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sub>/Co/Ta/Ru were proposed. Normalized magnetization hysteresis loops were obtained using polar magneto-optical Kerr effect (MOKE) measurement technique.

articleTitle: Analysis of unipolar leakage flux in series-hybrid permanent magnet machines
abstract: A series-hybrid variable flux memory (VFM) machine employing two different kinds of permanent magnets (PMs) on alternate rotor poles is investigated. This machine features controllable PM flux and good flux-weakening capability, as well as improved torque density. However, the unipolar end leakage flux occurs when the fluxes produced by two different kinds of PMs are not balanced. articleTitle: A detector-aware LDPC code optimization for ultra-high density magnetic recording channels
abstract: Aiming at further increasing the data-storage density beyond 1Tb/in<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>[1-3], bit-patterned media recording (BPMR), shingled writing (SW)/two-dimensional magnetic recording (TDMR) have emerged as new promising technologies. However, with the reduction of the track pitch, inter-track interference (ITI) becomes a major impairment for these magnetic recording systems. ITI combined with the conventional (down-track) inter-symbol interference (ISI) forms a two-dimensional (2D) interference that severely degrades the performance of data storage systems. Motivated by the superiority of data-storage density, large attention has been turned to 2D-ISI channels. Although the symbol-based Bahl-Cocke-Jelinek-Raviv (BCJR) 2D detector (2D-DET) [2] - hereinafter called full 2D channel detector-can provide optimal detection over such 2D-ISI channels, it has prohibitive complexity for the typical 2D data size. In [4], the well known suboptimal 2D-DET, iterative row-column soft decision feedback algorithm (IRCSDFA), has been further simplified using Gaussian approximation, the resultant simplified 2D-DET is referred as “GA-IRCSDFA”. Besides 2D channel detection, coding also provides a means to combat 2D-ISI. In [2], new low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes optimized for 2D-ISI channels detected using the 2D BCJR detector have been designed, and are shown to achieve better performance than LDPC optimized for additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channels. LDPC codes optimized for 2D-ISI channels detected using 2D GA-IRCSDFA detector in [5], exhibit excellent error-correction capabilities, especially for high codeword lengths. However, the ISI-optimized LDPC codes are designed for a 2D-ISI channel detected by the specific 2D-DET, and code optimization procedure should be operated again for a new detector. Moreover, the 2D-DET EXIT curve cannot be expressed in closed form, need to be evaluated by Monte Carlo simulation, statistically averaged over a large number of 2D detection simulationsIn this paper, we present a detector-aware LDPC code optimization method for a 2D-ISI magnetic recording channel, adjusting the variance of the 2D-ISI channel log-likelihood ratios (L-values) according to the specific 2D-DET. The new variance builds a new bridge of LDPC code optimization between the ISI-channel and AWGN channel. Specifically, the a-posteriori mutual information of the 2D-DET is calculated. Then we re-model the distribution of L-values as an approximately Gaussian N(μ,2μ)based on the estimated mutual information of the 2D-DET. Finally, we can re-use the code optimization methods employed in the AWGN channel employing the new variance of L-values from the corresponding 2D-DET in 2D-ISI channels, instead of the original variance.

articleTitle: Non-linear magnetic modeling of aircraft variable frequency synchronous generators
abstract: it is essential for manufacturers of aircraft electrical equipment to accurately model major components such as variable frequency synchronous generators (VFSG) prior to integration in an aircraft electrical power system. A particular problem is the trade-off between simulation speed and accuracy when non-linear windings are considered, and this paper considers the impact of non-linear magnetic behaviour on the overall model of a synchronous generator when approximations such as the well known DQ0 axis approach are used. This paper shows a hybrid approach to address this problem by including both winding non-linearities and a three stage VFSG model using DQ0 axis transformations to ensure correct THD behaviour without using a full ABC approach.

articleTitle: Decoupling control for a magnetic levitation wind turbine using neural network inverse scheme plus model reference adaptive controllers
abstract: As one of the well-known renewable energy resources, wind energy, which attracts a larger part of today's total investments, is now playing an increasingly important role around the world.Because the high cost and vulnerability of the gearboxes in wind turbines, the direct-drive wind turbines without gearboxes were replaced with the traditional wind turbines by the manufactures in recent years. But the threshold wind velocity of direct-drive wind turbines is higher than the traditional wind turbines, because of the size and weight of the direct-drive wind turbines. In addition, the working condition of wind turbines is very bad, such as heat, high humidity and impact loading. So the magnetic bearings with well performance of sealing, lubrication, shock resistance and long-lifetime can used in the direct-drive wind turbines to solve these problems mentioned above. The magnetic suspension system is a time variation system with multivariable, close coupling and nonlinear, which consists of some magnetic suspension devices such as magnetic bearings, suspension windings and so on. So the magnetic levitation control technology is difficult and complex in magnetic suspension system. The individual controllers with traditional linear control scheme, i.e., the proportional-integral-differential (PID), were used in magnetic suspension system, ignored the coupling between the variables in system. In order to realize high accuracy and high performance of the magnetic suspension system, the high-performance decoupling control is necessary in suspension system. Many control methods were put forward by some scholars around the world. The control of H∞ extension and Fuzzy were used in vehicle active suspension system. LQG control was used in Low bandwidth active suspension system. The internal model control system is used in bearingless permanent magnet synchronous motor by Sun xiaodong. The neural network inverse (NNI) system technology is advancing fast in different fields. For complex nonlinear systems, the NNI control scheme can play a role in feedback linearization and multi-variable decoupling, and this idea is simple and easy to understand. On the other hand, some uncertainties are inherent in nonlinear systems due to modelling error, loading changing and environment. The model reference adaptive (MRA) control is used in the nonlinear systems, where the tracking signal comes from a set of reference dynamics. So the NNI and MRA control can be adopted in the 5-DOF magnetic suspension system.

abstract: Bit-patterned media recording (BPMR) has been developed into an aggressive technology for the next-generation of hard disc drives (HDDs), aiming to extend storage density as well as to integrate into an HDD [1]. One of the major challenges in BPMR system is two-dimensional intersymbol interference (2D ISI), i.e. one-dimensional (1D) ISI from neighbor bits and intertrack interference (ITI) from adjacent tracks. From a signal processing view point, 2D detection schemes are required for these systems. However, it has been also shown that the direct 2D detection is NP-complete [2]. In other words, it is difficult to realize a 2D trellis detection for 2D ISI channels. One of the potential approaches is that we should create low complexity 2D detection solutions based on 1D schemes, but still reached near optimal performances of 2D detection schemes. In this research, we are interest in a solution of a twin iterative detection scheme based on 1D detector and decoder, applied for BPMR systems.

abstract: Summary form only given. The increasing importance of e-mobility will significantly enhance the amount of permanent magnets (pms) required for electric motors.
