In previous work, direct magnet recycling was mainly performed on low coercivity starting material (H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> ~ 1200 kA/m) [3-6]. Via powder metallurgical route and NdHx additions, the magnetic properties of the starting material could be approximately fully recovered in the recycled magnets [3, 4, 6]. Using DyH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> additions the coercivity of the recycled magnet even exceeds the coercivity of the starting material, however, remanence and maximum energy product are significantly reduced [5]. Higher coercivity starting material (H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> ~ 2000 kA/m) so far has been tested only by Li et al. [7] and Zakotnik et al. [2]. They produced recycled magnets by mixing with 24 wt% Nd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>PrFe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sub>B RE rich alloy and 1.9 wt% (Nd,Pr)H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>, respectively. Reported processes usually contain jet milling technique, hydrogenation process and isostatic pressing of powders [2-4,7]. Also, low energy ball milling in hexane was used [5,6]. In this work, we focus on the microstructure development during processing of recycled sintered magnets. The resulting microstructure and occurring kind and amount of phase constituents, which can be quantified by means of quantitative image analysis, sensitively depend on chosen parameters for milling and sintering procedure. The parameters partly behave in the opposite direction which is also reflected in the resulting magnetic properties. For magnetto-magnet recycling, a high coercivity Fe-Nd-B based pm (9 wt% Dy) well-suited for elevated temperatures was used as starting material (H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> = 2625 kA/m). Solely new Nd-rich Fe-Nd-B as-cast alloy (Fe-26Nd-7B) without intermixing hydride addition (e.g. NdH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>) was used for blending. The as-cast alloy was synthesized in an arc furnace operating in a highly clean Ar atmosphere. The chosen as-cast alloy consists of primary solidified T1 (Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sub>Nd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>B, hard magnetic Φ-phase), secondary solidified T1 and T2 (Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>Nd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.1</sub>B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>, paramagnetic η-phase) and the ternary eutectic E2 (Nd, T1, T2). This is also in accordance with the liquidus phase projection of the ternary Fe-Nd-B system [8]. For production of the recycled sintered magnets a lab sinter facility was used. The pre-shredded material was ball-milled, mechanically sieved and transversally pressed in a pm field under inert gas atmosphere. The milling time of the starting material was systematically varied between 10 and 45 min. Ball-milling the as-cast alloy for 45 min yielded D50 = 5.7 μm. To mix the powders of starting material and of the as-cast alloy, the method of two-component sintering was used. To obtain optimum magnetic properties, 40 wt% of the as-cast alloy was added to the starting material. Compared to fabrication of new Fe-Nd-B sintered magnets, the sintering temperature for the recycling sintered magnets had to be increased by 40°C. The higher sintering temperature was necessary to reach a sufficient density of ~7.5 g/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The obtained density of the recycling magnets was ~ 98 % of the density of the starting material. The magnetic properties of the recycled magnets was measured as H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> = 1883 kA/m, Jr = 1.1 T and (BH)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</sub> = 230 kJ/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> for a milling time of the starting material of 10 min, i.e. 72 % H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>, 98 % J<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> and 98 % (BH)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</sub> of the starting material, respectively. Although no Dy was added, 72 % of the original coercivity was recovered in the recycled magnet. In Fig. 1 the typical microstructure and domain structure of the three different recycled magnets is presented compared to the starting pm. In Fig. 2 the content of oxides and average grain sizes of the samples have been quantified by quantitative image analysis of statistically representative areas. The measured room temperature values of the coercivity are also shown. Accordingly, with increasing milling time, the coercivity is lowered. This may be due to both the increasing volume fraction of oxides (3.5 to 6.9 %) and to the simultaneously decreasing grain sizes with increasing milling time, i.e. the increase of surface to volume ratio of the powder particles. Additional grain boundary phase will be needed for complete wetting of the whole grain surfaces for larger milling times. The reduced remanence of the recycled magnets originates from the slightly reduced density. Because of the higher sintering temperature used, recycled magnets show slightly larger mean value of grain sizes compared to the starting material.

articleTitle: Description of statistical switching in perpendicular STT-MRAM within a numerical micromagnetic framework
abstract: The magnetization switching driven by spin-transfer torque (STT) [1] and Spin Hall effect (SHE) [2] is the fundamental dynamics to design magnetic memories and spin-logic devices.

articleTitle: Inhomogeneous parametric pumping of spin-waves by acoustic waves in an yttrium-iron-garnet film
abstract: Parametric amplification and generation of spin-waves has been a proven tool to study fundamental nonlinear effects in spin-waves [1].

articleTitle: Magnetic bearing with uniaxial control using radial layers repulsive type magnetic bearing
abstract: The magnetic bearing represents a solution for devices like flywheel for energy storage, maglev, or artificial heart since it levitates the rotor with no mechanical contact, minimizing energy losses due to friction and the wear of bearing parts.

articleTitle: Quadruple butterfly coil with passive magnetic shielding for focused Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation
abstract: Summary form only given. Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (TMS) is a non-invasive, safe and promising therapy for neurological conditions which utilizes transient magnetic fields for inducing electric field in the brain.

articleTitle: Spin Transfer Torque driven dynamics of the synthetic antiferromagnetic reference layer of perpendicular MRAM devices
abstract: Spin Transfer Torque Magnetic Random Access Memories (STT-MRAM) are based on Magnetic Tunnel Junctions (MTJs) made out of two ferromagnetic electrodes separated by a MgO tunnel barrier. Here we report experimental data of the STT-induced dynamics of a SAF RL in perpendicularly magnetized STT-MRAM devices. We show evidence of different RL dynamical modes depending on the SAF properties. We also develop an analytical model based on a 3-layer macrospin model, which allows us to reproduce the main feature of the experimental data and to derive a phase diagram of the RL dynamics. Experimental data of RL dynamics are obtained using time-resolved resistance measurements of individual MRAM devices.

articleTitle: Comparative study of E-core and C-core modular PM linear machines with different slot/pole combinations
abstract: Permanent magnet linear synchronous machines (PMLSMs) have attracted increasing interest due to their special merits, such as direct linear motion, fast dynamic response, simple system structure and so on. In order to simplify the manufacture and improve the fault-tolerant ability, two modular PMLSMs with C-core and E-core armature structures are presented and compared in this paper. The rotating modular PM machines with flux gaps are investigated [1], and it is shown that the performance can be improved if slot number is lower than the pole number. However, to modular PMLMs, the odd poles, i.e, 12s/13p, should be investigated, and the influence on detent force also should be analyzed.

articleTitle: Formalism and finite element study of actuator with toothed coupling
abstract: Toothed coupling machines and multi-air gap machines are interesting solutions for direct drive because of the high specific performances they can achieve.

articleTitle: Relationship between iron loss and pole-pair number in flux-switching permanent-magnet machines
abstract: Recently, flux-switching permanent-magnet (PM) (FSPM) machines have received considerable attentions recently in high reliability applications, due to its high power density, robust structure, and essential sinusoidal back-electromotive-force waveforms [1].

articleTitle: Modular dual three-phase fractional-slot overlapping windings for reducing rotor losses of permanent magnet synchronous machines
abstract: Due to high torque density, low torque ripple, high efficiency, excellent fault-tolerance capability and convenient manufacturing, fraction-slot concentrated windings (FSCWs) are desirable to be used in high performance permanent magnet (PM) synchronous machines.

articleTitle: Goos-Hänchen shift of a spin-wave beam in transmission through interface between two ferromagnets
abstract: The main object of investigation in magnonics, spin waves (SWs) are magnetization excitations propagating without charge transport.

articleTitle: Heat Assisted Recording: Advances in recording integration
abstract: With the recent 1.0 [1] and 1.5 [2,5] Tb/inch<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> basic technology demonstration and drive level demonstration [3,4], Heat-Assisted Magnetic Recording (HAMR) [5] has proven to be a viable and promising technology for future magnetic data-storage products.

articleTitle: Air-gap force and vibration of an advanced PM vernier machine
abstract: The vernier permanent magnet (VPM) machines have been widely studied in recent years due to their high torque density. In this paper, the air-gap force density and vibration of an advanced VPM machine is analyzed and compared to a conventional 12-slot 10-pole PM machine using FEA and experimental test. Due to the flux modulation principle of the VPM machine, it has more harmonics in the air-gap magnetic and force density field than the CPM machine. As a consequence, the acceleration spectrum of the VPM machine is more abundant than that of the CPM machine, in spite that their peak amplitudes are close. On the other hand, the maximum deformation of the VPM machine is much smaller than that of the CPM machine, which is a potential advantage for the VPM machine.

articleTitle: Iron loss model under DC dias flux density considering temperature influence
abstract: DC bias flux density exists in many types of electrical machines such as permanent-magnet synchronous machines (PMSM), brushless DC machines (BLDC) and switched reluctance motors (SRM), etc. Iron loss models under DC bias flux density at constant temperature are reviewed and evaluated by the ring specimen test in this study. In this study, the improved model is experimentally verified firstly by the ring specimen test at different alternating flux density, frequency, DC bias flux density and temperature.

articleTitle: Reduction of eddy current loss in flux-switching permanent-magnet machines using rotor magnetic flux barriers
abstract: In this paper, a new rotor structure with magnetic flux barriers will be designed for a five-phase 10/19-pole FSPM machine in order to reduce EC loss. The E-shaped laminated segments are adopted to build the stator. Also, fault-tolerant teeth (FTT) interleaving with armature teeth (AT) is adopted in this FSPM topology.

articleTitle: Towards realization of bulk L10-FeNi
abstract: One of the best candidates for Rare Earth-free magnets the L1<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> FeNi alloy is very attractive because it has a large uniaxial magnetic anisotropy energy (MAE) with Ku ∼ 1.3 ×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup>J/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, nearly the same saturation magnetization, μ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> = 1.59 T, as Nd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</inf>B, a high Curie temperature (>550 °C) and high corrosion resistance.

articleTitle: Multifunctionality of maghemite nanoparticles functionalized by HSA for drug delivery
abstract: Summary form only given. Multifunctional nanomaterials are finding considerale applications in medicine.

articleTitle: Modification of the field dependence and scaling of the magnetocaloric effect in LaFeSi across the tricritical point
abstract: The most straightforward classification of magnetocaloric materials is according to the order of the phase transition that they undergo: either second order (continuous) phase transitions (SOPT), like Gd, or first order magneto-structural phase transitions (FOPT) like the giant magnetocaloric material Gd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Ge<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>.

articleTitle: Analysis and testing of a hybrid Halbach magnetic gearbox
abstract: Magnetic gearboxes (MG) utilize magnetic field heterodyning to create speed change without physical contact. The object of this paper is to investigate the practical benefits of using this new hybrid Halbach (HH) structure in a MG. It should be mentioned that this analysis does not use magnets on the central modulation rotor. In this analysis the central modulation ferromagnetic rotor poles, are connected together using bridges. The addition of the bridges decreases the peak torque however it makes the construction of the MG significantly less challenging.

articleTitle: Modulating ring influence in dual air-gap magnetic gear electric machine and its improved structure using 3D printing; with FEA and experimental validations
abstract: Dual air-gap magnetic gear electric machines have been on the fore front of academic research in recent times [1]. This paper presents an analytical insight on the magnetic flux distribution inside the dual air-gap electric machine and will focus more on pointing out the influence of the modulating ring as the key structure in the dual air-gap electric machine. Furthermore, using 3D printing, an improved structure of the modulating ring is designed such that a cavity is created along the longitudinal centroid.

articleTitle: Development of Sm-Co permanent magnets
abstract: Samarium-cobalt alloys opened the era of the rare-earth permanent magnets, in which the energy density of magnets increased by a factor of ten in the first few decades.

articleTitle: A novel approach for plastic bonded magnets of the type MQU-F melt spun NdFeGaB-type alloys
abstract: Summary form only given. Herein, In order to increase the energy density in bonded magnets we introduce a novel technique we termed “plastic sintering”, an approach that simulates the classical sintering of magnetic powders of NdFeB, where a low melting Nd-rich non magnetic phase acts simultaneously as a wetting-bonding entity and as barrier to prevent magnetic interaction between the grains. The sintering is achieved at high temperatures in excess of 600 <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>C. In the proposed “plastic sintering” approach, we are aiming to achieve densities in excess of 80% at temperatures below 100 <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>C. We have employed a magnetic powder provided by Molycorp of the type MQU-F and as plastic binder MMA. We have coated a distribution of micron sized particles with a very thin <; 1 micrometer with MMA, dried and then subjected to compression up to 1.5 GPa. To polymerize the compressed powders we used a conventional furnace and a microwave furnace at around the polymerization temperature of 85 <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>C, for the conventional furnace for a period of 3 hours and for the microwave furnace for 10-15 minutes. There is no degradation of the coercivity, there is a reduction of the remanence magnetization proportional to the plastic coating, leading to densities of the order 82 % of the theoretical density. We will present the results from a series of experiments which show that: It is possible to plastic sinter MQU-F powders with a density in excess of 80 % Sintering time is at least ten times faster with microwaves compared to the conventional way. Care must be taken not to overheat the alloy, because it decomposes This approach is very promising for the formation of strong plastic bonded magnets with an energy product higher than the commercial ones.

articleTitle: Analysis of a Fall-back Transverse Flux Permanent Magnet Generator
abstract: In conventional Transverse Flux Permanent Magnet Generator (TFPMG) used for wind power application, the flux distribution in the U shaped stator core is uneven and also possesses very high magnetic flux leakages due to rotor inactive PM Poles.

articleTitle: Modelling of temperature dependence of saturation magnetisa-tion of silicon-iron steels
abstract: The temperature dependence of saturation magnetisation of commercial 0.1 to 3 wt. % silicon steels is first measured using an air-cored solenoid and then modelled using a linear formula in accordance with the spin-wave theory, over the range of 20-100°C and in 100 KA/m applied field. The samples measured were heated by applying a heavy ac current along their length, and the measurement of temperature was made using thermocouples. The paper discusses the effect of temperature variation on magnetisation in high field regime approaching saturation in several grades of electrical steel.

articleTitle: A novel design of the rotary electromagnetic actuator and the analysis of critical demagnetization state for its permanent magnet
abstract: The rotary type electromagnetic actuator is often used in the electromagnetic mechanical components design such as RF switch, signal electromagnetic relay, etc. Technical index of this type of actuator focus on high requirements for conversion speed, action frequency, signal reliability and the minimum volume under certain power. In this paper, a new type of rotary electromagnetic actuator with permanent magnet (PM) has been designed. Based on the PM polarity characteristics, it adopts double coil counterpoint control method and a ferro flux path is designed to optimize the magnetic circuit. The electromagnetic system and the contact system are designed individually, which can achieve a high level maximum space utilization. The migration analysis of the working point based on analytic model is carried on for the selection of PM. The precise static characteristics of the actuator is analyzed by a finite element model (FEM). The prototype actuator is assembled and tested. The advantages of fast conversion speed and high reliability is verified.

articleTitle: Ambient temperature influence on temperature of MCCB bimetal
abstract: Low voltage circuit breaker is the main switch electrical equipment of low voltage power supply and distribution system.In this paper, the ambient temperature influence on the temperature of MCCB bimetal is studied, which will be helpful for the follow-up study on the intelligent of MCCB. Fig. 1 (a) shows the picture of DZ47-60 and the 3D finite element model of DZ47-60 MCCB is established.

articleTitle: Control of interlayer exchange coupling and its impact on spin-torque switching of hybrid free layers with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy
abstract: Magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs) with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (PMA) have recently been studied for the scaling-down of spin-transfer-torque magnetic random access memory (STT-MRAM).

articleTitle: Capability characteristic analysis considering end-effect of linear induction motor using analytical method
abstract: Linear electric machines can generate a linear driving force, and therefore, are advantageous in a linear driving system. This paper deals with the analysis of performance characteristics of the linear induction motor (LIM) by using an analytical method such as the spatial harmonic method. LIM capability characteristics have been analyzed widely using both the finite element method (FEM) and the analytical method. However, in FEM analysis, the number of initial parameters used is often limited, and increasing the size of the initial model or changing the design parameters is not frequently done and is difficult in reality.

articleTitle: Effects of silicon content on properties of gas-atomized Fe-Si-Cr powders
abstract: Summary form only given. In this study Fe-Si-Cr powders with high Si content of 7, 8, 9 and 11% were gas-atomized and then effects of silicon content on the structural and magnetic properties of the Fe-Si-Cr powders were investigated on the emphasis of the order-disorder transition and the electrical resistivity. Gas-atomized Fe-Si-Cr powder was sieved to have a maximum and an average diameter of 30 and 14.38 mm, respectively. Subsequently the powder was annealed at 25-750 °C for 1 hour and then rapidly cooled. Crystal structure, surface morphology and magnetic properties were analyzed by XRD, SEM, VSM, impedance analyzer with 16454 A magnetic materials test fixture. In order to compare the electrical resistivity of the powder, the powders were compressed in a chamber and then the resistance was measured by 4 point probe method under a pressure of 12.9 MPa. Regardless of silicon content the morphologies of all the powders were spherical. However, the surface of a smaller powder (D >> 1.9 mm) is very smooth while that of a larger powder (D >> 9.6 mm) shows dendritic growth. The B2 phase appeared in all the as-atomized powders while the transformation to DO3 phase depends on the Si composition and annealing temperature. The temperature of the transformation to DO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> phase of 7, 8, 9 and 11% were 550, 450, 450 and 25 °C, respectively. The sizes of the DO3 phases of the Fe-7, 8, 9, 11%Si-Cr powders were 18.3, 14.5, 20 and 41 nm, respectively, after 550 °C annealing. However in our previous study the DO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> phase could be clearly observed in TEM selective area diffraction patterns of the as-atomized Fe-9%Si-Cr powder even though its intensity was very weak. Lattice parameter of the Fe-7, 8, 9%Si-Cr powders decreased with increasing annealing temperature while those of the Fe-11%Si-Cr powders were nearly constant. Coercivities of the Fe-7, 11%Si-Cr powders decrease abruptly after annealing 250 and 550 °C annealing, respectively while those of the Fe-8, 9%Si-Cr powder did not showed abrupt decrease and there were an increase after 450 °C annealing instead. The coercivity of the Fe-8%Si-Cr powder was lowest among them. Permeability decreased abruptly with annealing temperature except the Fe-11%Si-Cr powder. Highest permeability could be obtained in the Fe-8%Si-Cr powder after 250 °C annealing. It seems that high electrical resistivity rather than lower coercivity increased the permeability of the Fe-8%Si-Cr powder. With increasing operating frequency electrical resistivity of the soft magnetic materials becomes more and more important. The resistivity of rapidly cooled Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">87</sub>Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sub> alloy is three times higher than that of slowly cooled alloy. It was also reported that large difference in the electrical resistivity of Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">87.8</sub>Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12.2</sub> alloy was attributed from the factor that the rapidly cooled alloys consisted of the DO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> phase with short-range order whereas the slowly cooled alloys consisted of the DO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> phase with long-range order. Because the anti-phase boundary makes electrons scattered and thus increases the electrical resistance, the powder consisting of the DO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> phase with short-range order will have larger anti-phase boundary area and thus higher electrical resistivity. It seems that the lower permeability of the powder annealed at higher temperature is due to the decreased resistivity even though the lower coercivity was shown after high temperature annealing. It should be noted that the permeability of the Fe-11%Si-Cr powder is very low and nearly constant although the coercivity decreases very much with increasing annealing temperature. High resistivity of the powder annealed at lower temperature could be verified in the resistance measurement of the powder. As a conclusion the size and distribution of the DO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> phase determines the electrical resistivity and thus the permeability of the Fe-Si-Cr SMC.

articleTitle: FMR measurements of highly bismuth-substituted neodymium iron garnet thin films
abstract: A magnetic imaging technique that visualizes magnetic field in high-frequency up to GHz is strongly required as a frequency in electronics applications increases rapidly.

articleTitle: On local sensing of Spin Hall effect in tungsten film by using STM-type tunneling
abstract: The experimental study of the Spin Hall effect (SHE) has recently attracted much attention due to its promising technological applications in the area of spintronics [1–4].

articleTitle: Iron loss calculation for high-speed PM machine based on 3D orthogonal magnetic field
abstract: In recently years,the increasing attention has been given to high speed drives for wider range of industrial applications, such as flywheel energy storage, compact micro generation gas turbines, aircraft electrical starter-generator systems and compressors [1].

articleTitle: Comparative study of microfabricated inductors / transformers for high frequency power applications
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study on different microfabricated inductors (microtransformers), which are suitable for high frequency power application. Two different microtransformer designs with different magnetic core materials are considered in this work. The core materials used in this work are NiFe45/55 and CoFe. Also, two types of device packages are developed, namely QFN and FR4 embedded packages. For device testing, different high frequency switching regulators available on the market are used. This study shows the influence of different parameters on the performance of a certain high frequency application. In this paper, we discuss the influence of the design, magnetic material, and package type on the efficiency of the power application.

articleTitle: A disturbance compensation control for linear resonant actuator based on the law of energy conservation
abstract: Linear resonant actuators (LRAs) have been used in a wide range of applications because they can reciprocate in a comparatively short stroke in spite of their compact size and light weight.compensation. In this paper, we propose a load estimation method based on the law of energy conservation. Additionally, we propose disturbance compensation control that compensates load disturbance by using an estimated load. The effectiveness of the proposed control is verified through finite element method (FEM) analysis.

articleTitle: Preparation of the Zn-Al coating with high corrosion resistance on the sintered NdFeB magnets
abstract: Summary form only given. Sintered NdFeB permanent magnets possess outstanding magnetic properties such as high coercive force and high energy products. In this study a new kind of protective coating is developed on NdFeB magnets surface.During the experiment zinc-aluminum coating firstly is prepared by the dipping and centrifuging method, then preheated at 373K for 15minutes in the furnace. Finally, under the high temperature conditions of 583K the coating is baked for 30 minutes.The morphology texture of the Zn-Al coating is observed by SEM. The phase structure of the Zn-Al coating is analyzed by XRD.

articleTitle: Optimal current trajectory control of PMSM considering cross saturation effects
abstract: This paper proposes a current trajectory control strategy considering cross coupling and magnetic saturation effect under voltage and current constraint. It introduces geometric positions of torque and voltage increment in dq axis framework to determine the differentials between target values and results of the previous iteration, and then converts the torque and current differentials into current modification vector toward the optimal destination. It validated the proposed control strategy is insensitive to parameters variation and has well dynamic performance, it also can realize the seamless switch between constant torque control to flux-weakening control smoothly.

articleTitle: Thermal analysis of consequent-pole hybrid vernier permanent-magnet machine for EV/HEV applications
abstract: Summary form only given. Since vernier permanent-magnet machine (VPMM) has the merit of low-speed operation with high output torque due to the “magnetic-gearing” effect, they have been used in the direct-drive applications such as wind power generator, electric vehicle/hybrid electric vehicle (EV/HEV). The paper focuses on the thermal analysis of a consequent-pole HEVPMM (CP-HEVPMM) using FVM based on the losses distribution in the machine. Since, the DC field windings located between the modulation poles and are close to PMs, it will result in high temperature and have a negative influence on the PMs. The temperature field analysis of CP-HEVPMM depends on on the distributions of copper loss in DC field windings and armature windings, eddy current loss and iron loss. The loss and temperature distribution analysis in both low-speed and highspeed operation should be taken into consideration in the CP-HEVPMM design.

articleTitle: Evaluation method for multi-degree-of-freedom spherical actuators under power control
abstract: Multi-degree-of-freedom (multi-DOF) actuators have been developed for the fields of robotics and industrial machinery. In this paper, we proposed an evaluation method that can evaluate the static characteristics of multi-DOF spherical actuators under constant power. In this method, the torque area of the actuator is obtained from the torque equation, and this area is used for static characteristics evaluations. This makesmakes it possible to evaluate a torque around an arbitrary axis which is a feature of the spherical actuator. In the future, we are planning to propose torque area method under allowable current and the difference between the two methods.

articleTitle: Modeling of effective anisotropies in FeCo and Co nanowires
abstract: The knowledge of the basic magnetic properties of nanowires is very important for technological applications such as spintronic and sensing devices.Here we report on the evaluation of the effective anisotropies in Co-based nanowires such as CoFe, monocrystalline hcp Co and polycrystalline Co by means of micromagnetic simulations.The employed method is based on the magnetization torque simulations.We have retrieved the experimental shapes of the torque curves and shown that non-harmonic forms observed at low fields correspond to the presence of open vortices at the nanowire ends.

articleTitle: Effect of current annealing on magnetic anisotropy in glass-coated amorphous microwires with positive magnetostriction
abstract: The magnetoimpedance (MI) effect is known as a large and sensitive change in a voltage measured across a magnetic conductor carrying a high frequency current. In the present paper, we propose current annealing with the aim to establish a specific magnetic anisotropy of a helical type, which is important to enhance the MI sensitivity at microwave frequencies, or to realize pulsed MI for such applications as Magnetoresistive Random Access Memory (MRAM). Co-rich amorphous wires may have a small positive magnetostriction and almost bistable type of magnetization behavior. Our work concerns hysteresis loop and MI measurements before and after passing dc current in the wires under the study for 15, 30, 45, 60 and 75 minutes. The used current was passed in Co-based microwires with a total diameter of 29.5 μm and a core diameter of 23.9 μm and fixed at 26 mA in this study. In Figure 1 we present hysteresis loop variation without and with current annealing at different times, 15 minutes and 75 minutes. One can see that the magnetization behavior changed from bistable type which is typical for axial anisotropy to that occurring for helical anisotropy. As a result, the impedance at MHz frequencies may show a hysteresis of a bistable type, and at GHz frequencies the impedance remains sensitive to applied magnetic field and tensile stress. Yet, we can conclude that the dc current treatment is interesting enough for enhancing magnetic properties and for the development of magnetic-field sensors which is prominent in soft magnetic materials.

articleTitle: Core loss analysis of high speed motor by using vector magnetic characteristic
abstract: In order to design a high-efficiency motor, the iron loss that is generated in the motor core should be reduced. In this paper, the usefulness of the electrical steel sheet of 0.08 mm thickness as the motor core for a high speed motor is shown by using the magnetic measurement and the magnetic field analysis. The measured results show iron loss distributions by using thermography camera. This method has been applied to the surface mounted permanent magnet (PM) motors, which are removed stator windings, to measure temperature distributions on the stator surface during the PM rotor is rotating. When the revolution of motor becomes higher, the iron loss usually increases in a stator core due to the increase of eddy current. However, the core loss in the stator core with 0.08 mm thickness sheet under high evolutions slightly increases in comparison with 0.35mm thickness sheet.

articleTitle: Magnetic composite based magneto hydrodynamic pump
abstract: In this work, an NdFeB isotropic magnetic powder - polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) composite is used as the magnetic flux source for the MHD pump. MHD pumps can only pump conductive fluids. While liquid metals such as mercury or gallium can be used as the conductive fluid, for most commercial applications saline fluids, such as blood, urine or sea water serve as the conductive medium. During the functioning of a saline fluid MHD pump, chlorine gas is evolved at the anode, which results in corrosion. Thus, cheaper metals such as copper and aluminum cannot be used as electrodes in such pumps. Electrodes made up of noble metals such as Gold and Platinum have been used, but they drive up the system cost and also need specialized fabrication processes for adequate sidewall coverage. Herein, CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> laser printing is used to convert the insulator polyimide (PI) to conductive graphene and this material is used as the electrode. A polyimide precursor is spun coated on a silicon wafer and thermally cured to form an 8 μm thick polyimide film. Selective printing of the CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> laser across the surface of the PI film with a speed of 92 mm/s and power of 3 W forms the laser induced graphene (LIG) electrodes.

articleTitle: Effect of finite tunneling magneto-resistance for the switching dynamics in the spin transfer torque magnetic tunneling junctions
abstract: Summary form only given. The details of switching behavior of spin transfer torque magnetic random access memory (STT-MRAM) are important for the scientific understandings as well as the technical reasons. In order to understand the spin dynamics during the switching process, micromagnetic simulations are essential tool. However, most of micromagnetic simulations for the switching behavior of STT-MRAM assumed uniform current density for within the entire junction area, which is not true when the tunneling magneto-resistance (TMR) becomes larger. Since the MgO based TMR is typically more than 100 %, and even larger TMR is required for better performance. It is well known that the spin configuration of free layer is not collinear and the spins form a complex structure during the switching. Since the resistances between free and fixed layers are varied as a function of the angle between them, the local current density is also changed. Since the circuit for the STT-MRAM is operated by constant voltage mode, the current distribution is varied as a function of the free layer spin configurations, and the local current density is determined by a function of the local spin angles. In this study, we employed the embedded OOMMF script scheme, where OOMMF can be called by the main program. In the main program, we run OOMMF for short time (10 ps) and we calculate the angles between free and fixed layers according to the OOMMF result. Based on these spin configurations, we update local current density as an input file for the next step OOMMF. With the embedded OOMMF scheme, we can successfully calculate the non-uniform current density STT switching behavior due to the finite TMR. Since the non-uniformity of current density is strongly dependent on the TMR value, we plotted normalized Mz as a function of time for various TMR values in Fig. 1 (a) and (b). For the constant voltage operation mode, the resistance of anti-parallel configuration is larger than the parallel configuration because of finite TMR, so that the current density of anti-parallel configuration is smaller than that of parallel case for a given constant voltage. For the parallel to anti-parallel switching case, the shorter switching time for the larger TMR cases is obtained compared to zero TMR, because the current density is larger than zero TMR case. As a result the faster switching time is obtained for larger TMR as shown in Fig. 1 (a). However, for the anti-parallel to parallel switching case, the finite TMR will increase switching time. Note that the switching does not occur for the large enough TMR (>0.9) shown in Fig. 1 (b). It implies that the switching current density can be affected by the TMR values. We reported the TMR dependent switching behavior of STT-MRAM, which is usually discarded in many studies under the assumption of uniform current density. For the constant voltage mode, it is true that the current is a function of the angle between the magnetization directions of free and fixed layer. We clearly show that the larger TMR leads more non-uniform current density, and it changes the detail spin dynamics in STT-MRAM switching.

articleTitle: Core loss prediction in magnetic laminations under high-frequency trapezoidal induction waveform
abstract: Accurately estimating the core power losses under the trapezoidal induction waveform, and analyzing its variation with the duty cycle, are essential for the elaborate design of high-frequency transformers used in dual-active-bridge (DAB) dc-dc converters. In this paper, core power losses under trapezoidal induction waveform are theoretically predicted by considering the specific role of hysteresis, classical and excess loss components. The fixed coefficients for a wide frequency spectrum up to 10kHz of validity for the prediction of the hysteresis, classical and excess loss components are calculated by using a polynomial regression analysis. The results are confirmed through measurement.

articleTitle: Precision power measurement of spin-torque nano-oscillators using an accurate de-embedding structure and analysis
abstract: Summary form only given. Spin torque oscillators (STOs) have been an important area of research for the past decade due to their promise as nanoscale signal sources in GHz frequency range. One of the limitations of STOs has been their low output power. Many advances have been made in increasing the output power <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1-4]</sup>, however reported power is based on the value measured on test equipment, typically a spectrum analyzer, and does not represent the actual power delivered by the STO, which can be significantly higher. This discrepancy is caused by the lack of a proper model for the electrode structure. Therefore, it is essential to establish a physically sound model for the electrode structure in order to accurately estimate the maximum output power of the STO and optimize the electrode structure to make the most of the STO. In this work, we measured 24 independent devices across a wafer containing 140 Magnetic Tunnel Junction (MTJ) STOs, Fig. 1(a), and demonstrate an algorithm to accurately remove the influence of the electrode structure, an approach known in microwave engineering as de-embedding, of each STO using a simple three structure measurement technique. Our method is applicable to all STOs types, including giant magnetoresistive (GMR) and MTJ devices. Previous attempts at modeling electrode structures from S-parameter measurements have relied on ad-hoc models that simply try to “fit” measurements, rather than determine a systematic, physical representation of the electrode structure. In this work we show an equivalent model of the electrode structure, which reflects its physical behavior, that is able remove loss and parasitics of the electrode structure of all STOs across the wafer. Topology of the equivalent model of the embedding network is initially assumed based on the physical layout of the structure and component values are extracted from microwave S-parameter measurements. Fig. 1 (b) shows how parasitics of both the conductor layers on signal and return paths as well as the substrate conductivity is reflected in the topology of the equivalent circuit model. All of these are needed to estimate component values of the equivalent circuit model. Their values are determined from an OPEN and a THRU structure that are fabricated on the same wafer as the STO devices and are shown in Fig. 1(c). Using the S-parameters measurements of these two standards, we calculated the V-parameters and used them to systematically determine the values of each component of our proposed model. Once values are estimated, their effect is de-embedded (the loss and parasitcs removed) from 24 different MTJ STO devices with different diameters across the wafer. For demonstration, 10 of the measured devices before and after de-embedding are shown in Fig. 1(d). All devices exhibit pure resistive behavior as expected after de-embedding. Devices which are shown with red traces have lower substrate isolation, which is exhibit a low frequency resonance. As can be seen, the de-embedding is able to remove this loss and parasitics (frequency dependance) from the measurements across the entire wafer. In addition to the equivalent circuit based de-embedding, we also analyzed the potential loss of STO electrode structures through full 3D electromagnetic simulations in Ansys HFSS. Fig. 2(a) shows the structure which is simulated. We examined different conductor thickness and substrate conductivities. Fig. 2 (b) and (c) show the simulated results. The top metal layer is deposited using Au and it is often thin due to complexities of the fabrication of these nanoscale devices. The results show that if the thickness of the top Au layer falls below 80 nm, it will have a noticeable impact on power loss. More significant, however, is the effect of substrate conductivity. Simulations show that non-insulating substrates can cause up to 6 dB (75%) power loss in the measurement structure alone. This is surprising, as most fabrication methods have been agnostic to the substrate as it is often seen simply as a mechanical carrier wafer, rather than part of the electrical system.

articleTitle: Strain reconfigurable coupling of spin waves in width modulat-ed magnonic crystal waveguide
abstract: Summary form only given. Recent progress in the magnon-based electronics can be used as a signal carrier in the magnonic waveguiding structures operating in the GHz and THz frequency range. This paper reports on the experimental and numerical study of the SW propagation in the reconfigurable MC waveguide. Both the experimental measurement and numerical simulations show that the frequency of the center of the forbidden zone is f=5.348 GHz, which corresponds to the Bragg wavenumber k<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</sub>=125 1/cm. Using the interdigital SS electrode the doubling of the value of strain induced period and the increasing the modulation depth of the reconfigurable MC is possible. Thus the paper demonstrates that dual H-field and E-field tunability is the key advantage of strain tuned MC. Magnetic tuning can be performed through the variation of a bias magnetic field, while electric tuning is possible due to control of the properties of PZT layer through the variation of an applied electric field.

articleTitle: Miniature tri-axis magnetometer with in-plane GMR sensors
abstract: Summary form only given. In this work, a miniature 3D magnetometer with in-plant giant magnetoresistance (GMR) sensors and a fluxguide was designed, implemented and characterized. The sensors used are the antiferromagnetic giant magnetoresistance sensor, AA002, from Nonvolatile Electronics Corporation. The sensor dies are 3.4mm×0.4mm in dimension and the tube-shaped fluxguide is 4 mm in diameter and 3.4 mm in height. The fluxguide is aligned and attached to the center of three sensor dies to enhance the sensitivity as well as to enable the detection of out-ofplane field.

articleTitle: 3D interconnected magnetic nanofiber networks with multifunctional properties

authors.preferredName: T. da Câmara Santa Clara Gomes

abstract: Summary form only given. Track-etched polymer membranes with crossed nanochannels have been revealed suitable as template for the electrodeposition synthesis of 3D interconnected magnetic nanofiber networks that present interesting magnetic and magneto-transport properties [1-3]. As shown in Fig. 1, such crossed nanowires systems are mechanically stable and self-supported after dissolution of the porous template. In addition, magneto-transport measurements can be easily performed on such interconnected nanofiber network films, with the flow of current restricted along the nanowire segments. The successive track-etch process allows the control of the template geometry such as the angles between the nanochannels and template normal, the volumetric porosity and the mean diameter that can be tuned between few tens of nm to few hundreds of nm. The template is partially filled from a previously sputtered metallic cathode by an electrodeposition process allowing the control of the material composition and nano-structuration, such as nanowires, nanotubes, core-shell nanocables or multilayered nanowires. The cathode is then locally removed to create a two-probe design suitable for easy electric measurements, as shown in Fig. 1c. Magneto-transport measurements are performed by sweeping the external magnetic field along the out-of-plane (OOP - z axis in Fig. 1c) and the in-plane (IP - y axis in Fig. 1c) directions. The magnetic and magneto-transport properties of crossed homogeneous nanowires (CNWs) and multilayered nanowires, synthesized by pulsed electrodeposition technique from a single electrolyte solution, have been investigated in details. A close relation between the CNWs magnetic and structural properties has been demonstrated in Co CNWs networks where the magnetic anisotropy can be accurately controlled by changing the electrolyte pH [2,4]. The crystalline structure can be switched from fcc to hcp with either the c-axis parallel or perpendicular to the NW axis such that the shape anisotropy and crystal anisotropy can either add or compete. A similar behavior was found in NiCo CNWs depending on the alloy composition in agreement with previous results obtained on bulk materials and films [3,5,6]. Neglecting the crossing zones that have a much smaller volume fraction than the NWs, the shape anisotropy of the fcc Ni-rich CNW network leads to the alignment of the magnetization of the mono-domain NWs with the current flow along the NWs axis leading to the highest resistive state, as shown in Fig. 2a. The application of a magnetic field in the OOP or IP direction decreases the resistance due to the AMR effect. The magnetocrystalline anisotropy present in hcp Co-rich alloy systems prevents the system to reach this highest resistance state and is also highlighted by the decrease of the squareness of the normalized hysteresis curves shown in Fig. 2b. An analytical model inherent to the topology of 3D nanowire networks has been validated, allowing to extract the AMR values from the measured magnetoresistance curves along the OOP and IP directions [2-3]. The AMR ratio variation with respect to the Ni content shown in Fig. 2c for the NiCo CNWs has been found coherent with previous results obtained on bulk materials and films [3,7]. The large AMR ratio obtained around 75% atomic of Ni makes this system very attractive to explore the presence of domain walls at the crossing zones using AMR measurements. By increasing the NW diameter, the crossing zones have larger volume which give rise to complex domain wall effect at low field. Finally, interconnected Co/Cu and NiCo/Cu multilayered 3D NWs networks display large CPP-GMR responses measured with the current flowing perpendicularly to the plane of the layers in the individual nanowire segments and thus overall in the plane of the 3D network film. Other 3D nanofiber network architectures based on nanotubes and core-shell nanocables are currently investigated. A wide range of controllable parameters that can be used to tune the magnetic and magnetotransport properties of mechanically stable and self-supported3D interconnected nanofiber networks. Numerical simulations are in progress to provide a better understanding of the studied systems. These mechanically stable 3D nanofiber superstructures have potential applications in many fields.

articleTitle: Ferromagnetic resonance investigation of origins of the perpen-dicular magnetic anisotropy in Pd/Co bi-layer and Pd/Co/Pd tri-layer films
abstract: The interface perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (PMA) is known to be induced at the interface between a ferromagnetic metal (FM) layer and a non-magnetic (NM) heavy-metal layer such as Platinum or Palladium (Pd) in a FM/NM bilayer or multilayer film.In the present work, we grow Pd/Cobalt bi-layer and Pd/Co/Pd continuous tri-layer films on rigid silicon (Si, Young's modulus of 200 GPa) substrates and on flexible Kapton<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> (Kpt, Young's modulus of 4 GPa) and expose the grown films to hydrogen gas (H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) or elastic stress.The films are deposited with magnetron sputtering.We also investigate deformation (bending) of the films.

articleTitle: Investigation of bending stress effect in diagonal and off-diagonal GMI sensors
abstract: Giant Magneto-Impedance (GMI) sensors are very promising due to their high sensitivity. In this paper, a first study is realized to investigate the impact of this bending stress on a GMI sensor. The changes in the sensitivity and offset of the GMI sensor in both diagonal and off-diagonal configurations have been measured.

articleTitle: Optimisation of Co2MnSi thin films and multilayers for spin Seebeck devices
abstract: The spin Seebeck effect is defined as the generation of a pure spin current (J<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>) when a magnetised material is subjected to a temperature gradient (ΔT).To detect it, a thin non-magnetic layer [NM] such as Pt, is deposited on top of the material of interest. This converts the spin current, J<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>, into an observable thermoelectric voltage (VSSE) by way of the Inverse Spin Hall Effect (ISHE). It has been shown that this effect is linearly proportional to ΔT and the magnetisation of the magnetic layer. Experimentally realised in ferromagnetic insulators, the SSE has also been seen in ferromagnetic conductors (FMC) such as Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>MnSi (CMS). We are interested in how this phenomenon might be applied to harvesting waste heat (thermoelectric generators) or spintronics applications (spin current source). CMS has been proposed to exhibit half metallic behaviour at the Fermi Energy (Ef), where theory predicts 100% spin polarisation (SP), which has recently been backed up by spin-resolved spectroscopy work in thin films.

articleTitle: Design of LDPC codes for unequal ISI channels
abstract: In magnetic recording system, each track or sector may suffer different distortion and noise levels, for example, media noise, intersymbol interference (ISI)/inter-track interference (ITI), reader sensitivity (in case of multi-reader), resulting in unequal error rates or unequal ISI channels. A generic scenario is considered for the multi-read system whereby tracks with different areal densities experience unequal ISI and ITI levels, hence, different targets are used. In this work, the codeword of LDPC code is divided and transmitted in the unequal ISI channels. The aim of this scheme is to avoid transmitting the whole codeword in a high error rate channel. It resembles the diversity technique in wireless communication, which transmit the information over multiple-channel by multiple-antenna. In this work, we use the unequal ISI channels.

articleTitle: Contactless energy transfer: Magnetics and acoustics
abstract: Introduction Contactless energy transfer (CET) is used in many applications where a physical connection between a device and a power source is impractical or even impossible.

articleTitle: Design and basic spin wave dynamics of a dual band magnonic crystal
abstract: The use of spin waves (SW) in magnonic crystals (MCs) as information carriers has been the target of intense investigation in recent years, particularly in relation with the possibility of controlling their Bragg diffraction and dispersion relations by an applied field, and their peculiarity in the context of dissipationless computing, since SWs don't involve charge motion and ohmic losses. In this work, we investigate a special 2D Permalloy MC, designed in such a way that SWs can propagate in distinct regions of it, depending on the frequency band they belong to, so to guarantee complete signal independence. We characterize the two spin wave types, by determining the two localization areas and the extension of the corresponding bands. The basic idea is considering two superposed sublattices, and using shape anisotropy to differentiate in energy the dynamics within the two sublattice elements: in this way, the excitations corresponding to different sublattice elements are forced to belong to different frequency ranges.

abstract: Permanent Magnet Linear Motors (PMLMs) are widely applied in xy-positioning stages such as laser cutters, pick & place systems or vision inspection devices [1].
